protein: Aquifex aeolicus adenylate kinase (Adk), wild type
reference_state: Wild-type apo Adk, no ligand; 10 °C (perdeuterated) and 20 °C (protonated); pH 7.0, 40 mM MOPS, 50 mM NaCl (NMR buffer stated for the perdeuterated sample; the 20 °C protonated buffer is not stated separately)
literal_two_peak: does not: Authors call the 20 °C apo exchange fast with small amplitude; no regime stated at 10 °C, no apo Δω, and no minor-state peaks reported.
basis: Free wild-type Adk shows µs–ms exchange in the hinges and parts of both lids. No pA/pB or Δω is reported for apo; the authors say the small amplitude of the dispersion profiles hampered characterization of the nature of the transition. A population (95 ± 2% closed, minor state more open) is measured only for the Mg-Ap5A-bound enzyme.
kex: 950 ± 150 s-1 at 10 °C (AQADK-J1, AQADK-r1); 2,000–7,000 s-1 compatible range at 20 °C, no unique fit (AQADK-J2, AQADK-r2)
pB: not reported for apo; the authors say the small dispersion amplitude hampered characterization of the nature of the transition (AQADK-J1)
regime: Not stated at 10 °C. At 20 °C the authors call the apo exchange fast, with small amplitude ('the rate of exchange was fast'; too fast to suppress Rex at the highest CPMG field) (AQADK-J2, AQADK-r2). No apo Δω is printed.
residues: Hinges and parts of both lids (AMP lid 30–71 and ATP lid 111–169 are the lid domains as defined for TLS refinement, AQADK-J5, not the exchanging region). Exchanging residues are shown only as a colour map at 10 °C (Fig. 3c) and as selected curves at 20 °C (Supplementary Fig. S6), with no residue list (AQADK-J1, AQADK-J2).

structure_match.what: Closed Zn2+–Ap5A inhibitor complex. PRE from a spin label on the AMP lid of the apo Y52C construct broadens ATP-lid residues, which the authors read as closed-like distances when compared with the open apo substates and the inhibitor-bound structure. Labelled construct, no population or rate.

Apo crystal with three molecules (A, B, C) at different degrees of lid closure along the hinge path that the Ap5A complex completes. Crystal snapshots, no solution population or rate. The authors note the three substates seem to be stabilized by crystal contacts.

fallback_annotation: May have an alternate conformation differing at the hinges and parts of both lids (lid domains 30–71 and 111–169 as defined for TLS refinement), based on 15N TROSY CPMG relaxation dispersion of the apo enzyme plus PRE and smFRET on labelled constructs (doi:10.1038/nature06410).
other_conditions: Mg-Ap5A-bound WT, 20 °C: yes. kex 300 ± 150 s-1 with 95 ± 2% closed and a more open minor state; 46 residues carry fitted ΔωN (AQADK-J11, AQADK-r3).
Mg-ADP turnover, 20 °C: possible. kex 1,615 ± 100 s-1 (kclose 1,571, kopen 44 s-1), no population reported (AQADK-J8, AQADK-r9).
Mg-AMPPNP + AMP, 20 °C: possible. kex 1,410 ± 100 s-1; peak splitting at partial ligand saturation shows the slow opening step (AQADK-J10, AQADK-r10, AQADK-r12).
Mg-ADP turnover, 50 °C: exchange faster than 10,000 s-1 (lower bound, data not shown) (AQADK-J9, AQADK-r11).
Mg-free nucleotide-bound WT: no_evidence by CPMG; the authors state lid opening is too slow for the window, with no conditions or data given (AQADK-J13, AQADK-r19).

Apo Y52C/V145C dye-labelled construct (35% of WT activity), room temperature, smFRET: switching between open-like and closed-like distances, kopen 6,500 ± 500 s-1, kclose 2,000 ± 200 s-1 (AQADK-J7, AQADK-r5).
caveats: The closed-like identity of the apo minor state comes from labelled constructs (Y52C PRE, Y52C/V145C smFRET), so it is mutant-based inference; the PDB entries are crystal endpoints, not a solved minor state. the NMR collaborator is asked which sample the RelaxDB labels come from (10 °C apo, 20 °C apo or 20 °C Mg-ADP turnover). Homolog rows (E. coli, P. profundum, G. stearothermophilus Adk) were not used for the call.

protein: Limulus polyphemus arginine kinase, recombinant wild type
reference_state: Wild-type substrate-free arginine kinase, 25 °C (also 15–30 °C); pH 6.5, 10 mM sodium citrate, 50 mM KCl, 0.5 mM DTT; no nucleotide or Mg (2009/2011 samples). Methyl sample (2017): 10 mM potassium citrate, 50 mM KCl, pH not stated
literal_two_peak: does not: Authors assign intermediate exchange (α 1.1–1.3) to the three L8 residues used for pB; the minor state is seen only through dispersion and no minor-state peaks are reported.
basis: At 25 °C the free enzyme exchanges in four backbone regions. The 2009 collective 15N CPMG fits of the hinge, the NTD–CTD interface and loop L8 give a rate and a minor-state population, with the largest minor state in L8 (2.6 ± 0.6%). For dynamic domain 1 the text reports a collective fit with pB < 0.3% and 'unreasonably large Δω and errors', and the 2011 interface fit is indeterminate. A four-temperature fit and ILV methyl CPMG reproduce an L8 minor state of a few percent.
kex: 25 °C collective fits: loop L8 790 ± 60 s-1; NTD hinge 1,930 ± 350 s-1; NTD–CTD interface 800 ± 100 s-1; dynamic domain 1 790 ± 70 s-1 (Table 1) or 990 ± 110 s-1 (text) (ARGKIN-J1–J4, ARGKIN-r1). L8 530 ± 80 to 1,080 ± 150 s-1 from 15 to 30 °C, 860 ± 120 s-1 at 25 °C (the rate paired with the 4.9% L8 population, ARGKIN-r6) (ARGKIN-J9, ARGKIN-r4–r7). L170/L187 methyls 970 ± 38 s-1 (ARGKIN-J10, ARGKIN-r11).
pB: L8 2.6 ± 0.6%; hinge 0.4 ± 0.1%; interface 1.1 ± 0.1%; dynamic domain 1 0.4 ± 0.1% (Table 1; text: < 0.3%) (ARGKIN-r1). L8 3.5 ± 0.3% to 5.7 ± 1.6% from 15 to 30 °C, 4.9 ± 0.5% at 25 °C (with kex 860 ± 120 s-1), from E190, D192, T206 only (ARGKIN-r4–r7). L170/L187 methyls 4.8 ± 0.3% (ARGKIN-r11).
regime: Intermediate for L8 residues E190, D192 and T206 at 25 °C (α = 1.15 ± 0.22, 1.33 ± 0.34 and 1.12 ± 0.21), the subset used for pB in the four-temperature fit (ARGKIN-J9, ARGKIN-r4–r7); interface α ill-defined; apo methyls span 'slow, intermediate, and fast' (2017, ARGKIN-r11). Δω: Table 1 (2009) prints per-residue 15N |Δω| within the collective fits, hinge 3.2–4.4 ppm (D88, H90, G92), interface 0.9–3.8 ppm, dynamic domain 1 1.0–5.6 ppm, loop L8 0.6–2.4 ppm (ARGKIN-r1).
residues: NTD hinge D88, H90, G92; NTD–CTD interface D71, F136, N137, F270, C271, N274, G276, G332; dynamic domain 1 and hinge R126, C127, R129, V220, V222, R229, Q234; substrate-binding loop L8 I182–G209 (17 residues in the collective fit); methyls L170, L187, L219, I231, I210, L331

structure_match.what: Transition-state-analogue (closed) crystal structure. Apo solution RDCs and shifts fit a mixture of the 3M10 apo and 1M15 TSA endpoints with an apo fraction of about 0.5 (shifts) to 0.7 (RDCs), and the authors conclude that solution apo enzyme contains substrate-bound-like features. Static-average and dynamic-mixture models give very similar Q-values, so RDCs alone cannot tell them apart; relaxation dispersion gives an apo fraction > 0.97. Separately, the 2009 CPMG paper speculates that the L8 motion may sample the closed-form configuration (ARGKIN-r1).
Refined apo crystal structure, the open endpoint of the same RDC mixture. The RDC paper's Methods name the deposited model 3M15 once; elsewhere the paper uses 3M10.

fallback_annotation: May have an alternate conformation differing at loop L8 (I182–G209), the NTD hinge (D88, H90, G92), the NTD–CTD interface and dynamic domain 1, based on 15N TROSY CPMG and ILV methyl CPMG relaxation dispersion (doi:10.1016/j.str.2009.08.014; doi:10.1021/bi101664u; doi:10.1021/jacs.7b00236).
other_conditions: 15–30 °C, same buffer: yes. Interface 570 ± 120 to 1,440 ± 310 s-1 (population indeterminate) and L8 530–1,080 s-1 with 3.5–5.7% minor state (ARGKIN-J8, ARGKIN-J9, ARGKIN-r4–r7).
Michaelis complex analogue (arginine + Mg·AMPPNP), imidazole/Mg buffer: yes. kex 914 ± 15 s-1, excited state 3.10 ± 0.04% with TSA-like methyl shifts (ARGKIN-J17, ARGKIN-r12).

Transition-state analogue (arginine + Mg·ADP + nitrate): yes. Backbone 2,300–2,750 s-1 with domain 4 pB 1.3 ± 0.1% and domain 5 pB 1.8 ± 0.1% (ARGKIN-J20, ARGKIN-J21, ARGKIN-r15); methyls 4,247 ± 72 s-1 with pB 2.75 ± 0.05%, conditional on an assumed slope (ARGKIN-J18, ARGKIN-r13).
Product complex analogue (pAIE + Mg·ADP): possible. kex 4,690 ± 119 s-1, no population (ARGKIN-J19, ARGKIN-r14).
caveats: The L8 population depends on the residue subset (2.6% from all 17 residues versus 4.9% from three residues at 25 °C). Dynamic domain 1 has two inconsistent fits in the same paper, and its methyls exchange at 3,890 ± 29 s-1 (pB 0.56%), so methyls may report a different process; I210 suggests three or more states. All apo samples were in citrate with no citrate-free control, and bound samples switched to imidazole/Mg, so ligand and buffer change together. The RDC match to 1M15 cannot separate exchange from a static average.

protein: Mycobacterium tuberculosis β-lactamase BlaC, wild type
reference_state: Wild-type resting-state (free) BlaC, 298 K; pH 6.4, 94 mM sodium MES, 6% D2O, no phosphate
literal_two_peak: cannot tell: Δω and pB of the 860 s-1 process are undetermined; the authors call the four broadened amides 'intermediate to fast'; WT shows no peak doubling (doubling only in G132N and the clavulanate adduct).
basis: Free wild-type BlaC shows active-site millisecond exchange at about 860 s-1, but the authors could not determine the excited-state population or shift difference 'with any accuracy'. Four anion-site amides are broadened beyond detection; the authors calculate that the same process would need a minor state above 15% to do this, which is an estimate rather than a measured population.
kex: (8.6 ± 0.6) x 10^2 s-1 at 298 K, two-state model assumed, two-field (14.1 and 20.0 T) group fit of eight amides (BLAC-J1, BLAC-r1, BLAC-r4)
pB: not determined with any accuracy (authors; BLAC-J1, BLAC-r1); the authors' own Bloch-McConnell estimate is that pB must exceed 15% (with Δω > 0.1 ppm 1H and/or 1 ppm 15N at 20 T) if the four broadened amides share the 860 s-1 process (BLAC-J2)
regime: No regime stated for the 860 s-1 process (Δω not determined). For the four anion-site amides broadened beyond detection the authors write that 'an intermediate to fast exchange process may be present in the active site' (2020; BLAC-r1, BLAC-J2).
residues: Group fit: F68, C69, T71, E166, E168, N170, T215, A218 (named in Elings 2021 SI Table S3, doi:10.1128/aac.02628-20; BLAC-J1); broadened beyond detection: Ser70, Ser130, Thr235, Thr237 (Ambler numbering; entry 43, 101, 210, 212 by the project's alignment)
fallback_annotation: Shows millisecond exchange in the active site (kex ≈ 860 s-1, 15N TROSY CPMG at 14.1 and 20.0 T; group-fit residues F68, C69, T71, E166, E168, N170, T215, A218); minor-state population, shifts and structure not determined; no minor-state peaks observed. Ser70, Ser130, Thr235 and Thr237 are broadened beyond detection, by the same or a separate process (Elings 2020, doi:10.1128/aac.02025-19).
other_conditions: WT CEST at 288 and 298 K: no_evidence for exchange at 20–200 s-1 (BLAC-J3, BLAC-r2).

G132N mutant, 298 K, MES: yes. Doubled peaks, kex 88 ± 6 s-1, state B 40 ± 2%; the G132N crystal (PDB 7A74, grown with 100 mM sodium phosphate added, while the NMR was phosphate-free) shows double conformations, and the authors write that the X-ray and NMR observations 'may thus represent the same phenomenon' (BLAC-J14, BLAC-J17, BLAC-r6, BLAC-r9).
K234R mutant: no_evidence by 15N CPMG at 298 K (BLAC-J12, BLAC-r5).
Avibactam adduct: possible. kex (3.4 ± 0.2) x 10^3 s-1 from a single-field fit, no population (BLAC-J7, BLAC-r3).

Clavulanate adduct: unresolved. At least 21 amides split into peaks at relative occupancy 42 ± 3%; exchange between them was not measured, and the authors infer kex < 100 s-1 from the doubling (BLAC-J9, BLAC-r3).

Directed-evolution mutants in 100 mM phosphate: peak doubling read as slow exchange well below 50 s-1 (authors: '<<50 s−1'), populations not quantified (BLAC-J19, BLAC-r10); I105Y-S130G and I105G-G132N in phosphate: no_evidence by CPMG (BLAC-J21, BLAC-J22, BLAC-r12).
caveats: Whether the four broadened anion-site amides and the 860 s-1 process are one process or two is unresolved. In every BlaC crystal published as of 2020 those four side chains hydrogen-bond a ligand or a buffer anion, and MES (a sulfonate) was never compared with another buffer. Mutant NMR from 2024-2025 used phosphate, which binds the active site, so it is not like-for-like with the WT MES data. A cached SAXS study proposing an open apo shape has no evidence row and was not used.

protein: Human biliverdin IX-beta reductase (BLVRB), wild type
reference_state: Wild-type apo human BLVRB, 20 °C (also 10, 5, 0 °C); pH 6.5, 50 mM Bis-Tris, 50 mM NaCl, 1 mM DTT; refolded, coenzyme removed by reverse-phase chromatography (Resource 15RPC, 2018 methods; the step is not stated for the 2023 samples)
literal_two_peak: does not: Authors: exchange on the fast NMR timescale for the fittable residues; the minor state is seen only through dispersion and no second peak set is reported.
basis: Apo BLVRB shows µs–ms exchange at more than 30 residues around the three active-site loops and in the C-terminal lobe; the authors call the exchange fast for the residues they could fit (e.g. S111, L125). The 2023 grouped multi-temperature (0–20 °C, Arrhenius-constrained) fits give a rate and a minor-state population for two residue groups (about 2.2% and 1.2% at 20 °C), although the 2018 analysis found the population not separable in that regime and the 2023 authors call two-site fits 'an over-simplification'.
kex: Group II 1,088 ± 180 s-1 and Group III 3,797 ± 800 s-1 at 20 °C, slowing to 181 ± 66 and 850 ± 178 s-1 at 0 °C (BLVRB-J3, BLVRB-J4, BLVRB-r15–r18); per-residue S111 1,200 ± 300 s-1 and L125 2,200 ± 540 s-1 at 20 °C (BLVRB-J1, BLVRB-r1)
pB: reported as pA: 2023 Table 2 prints major fractions 97.8 ± 0.2% (Group II) and 98.8 ± 0.1% (Group III) at 20 °C, so pB = 2.2 ± 0.2% and 1.2 ± 0.1%; at 0 °C reported as pA = 95.5 ± 1.5% and 97.8 ± 0.3%, so pB = 4.5 ± 1.5% and 2.2 ± 0.3% (the 0 °C Group II cell prints no unit) (BLVRB-r15, BLVRB-r18); not separable in the 2018 fast-exchange fits (BLVRB-r1)
regime: fast NMR timescale for the residues that could be fit to the Carver–Richards equations (2018), with populations that 'cannot be accurately deconvoluted under such an exchange regime' (BLVRB-J1, BLVRB-r1). Δω: the 2024 per-residue refit prints ΔωN from 0.54 ± 0.11 ppm (D80) to 9.49 ± 0.96 ppm (G76) (SI Table S1, BLVRB-r38).
residues: Active-site loops 10–15, 76–82 and 109–114 (more than 30 residues at 20 °C); Group II L74, T77, C109, S111, Q126; Group III I154, G155, T164, I176, Y205

structure_match.what: NADP+-bound (holo) crystal. The authors report that apo and holo crystals differ at R35, R39 and the R78 clamp. Separately, apo CPMG shift differences show 'at least several weak correlations' with apo-to-holo CSPs (2023), so the apo enzyme may sample holo-like states; I176 and Y205, both in this row's residue list, do not. The holo-like reading comes from shifts, not from 1HDO coordinates; not a solved minor state.

fallback_annotation: May have an alternate conformation differing at the active-site loops (residues 10–15, 76–82, 109–114) and the C-terminal lobe (I154, G155, T164, I176, Y205), based on 15N TROSY CPMG relaxation dispersion at 0–20 °C (doi:10.1016/j.jmb.2018.06.015; doi:10.3389/fmolb.2023.1244587).
other_conditions: NADP+-bound, 20 °C: possible. Exchange quenched in the apo-exchanging loops except S111 and T164, and new exchange at D36, S37, R39, with no rate or population (BLVRB-J16, BLVRB-J17, BLVRB-r2).
NADPH- or NADP+-bound, 0–10 °C: yes. Grouped fits give rates and 1–5% minor states for Groups I–III, with population errors as large as the minor fraction for some NADPH groups (BLVRB-J19–J24).
NADP+ + bilirubin (commercial isomer mixture), 0–10 °C: Group II no_evidence; Groups I and III exchange (BLVRB-J25–J27).
Mutants R78A, T164A, T164I, T164S, S111A: exchange changes but persists (BLVRB-J33, BLVRB-J35–J39).
caveats: The population is model-dependent: not separable (2018 per-residue fits), about 1-2% (2023 grouped Arrhenius fits), or poorly determined in the 2024 per-residue refit, whose SI Table S1 prints pA from 50% to 99.8% with errors up to about ±22% and several values at exactly 50%, possibly a fit bound (our reading; BLVRB-r38). Without the reverse-phase step 1-3% of the enzyme stayed coenzyme-bound (authors, data not shown); that this fraction is similar in size to the fitted apo minor states is our inference. Rates in the 2023 and 2024 tables are printed in 'Hz' and are carried as s-1 without conversion.

protein: Escherichia coli CheY, wild type, unphosphorylated
reference_state: Wild-type unphosphorylated CheY without Mg2+ (1 mM EDTA), 15 °C; pH 7.0, 50 mM sodium phosphate, 0.02% NaN3; >80% 2H
literal_two_peak: cannot tell: the authors state no regime and report no minor-state peak. Computed from their Table 2 local fits (PMC3552614, 1 mM EDTA, 15 °C): D64 kex 96 ± 16 s-1, Δω 9.4 ± 1 ppm, minor fraction 0.20 and R19 kex 180 ± 30 s-1, Δω 5.7 ± 1 ppm, minor fraction 0.04 give kex/Δω 0.03 and 0.08 at 600 MHz, i.e. slow exchange that predicts a resolved minor peak; none is reported, so either the peak exists unreported or these local fits are unreliable (computed by Claude 2026-10-20 after the night review). All other fitted residues are intermediate or fast (kex/Δω 1.0-12.9).
basis: Without Mg2+, 13 active-site and FliM-face residues show µs–ms exchange, but no population of a defined minor state is reported. Per-residue two-state fits give local rates (96 to 2,440 s-1) and local fractions; group fitting eliminated all residues, and the authors state that CheY 'does not undergo a two-state concerted switch' and favour non-concerted, segmental switching.
kex: per-residue local fits, no shared value: 96 ± 16 s-1 (D64) to 2,440 ± 570 s-1 (V107) (CHEY-J1, CHEY-r1)
pB: reported as per-residue major fraction pI = 0.67 ± 0.2 (N94) to 0.99 ± 0.01, so local minor fractions 1 − pI = 0.33 ± 0.2 to 0.01 ± 0.01; local fit parameters, not a shared population; N94 is ill-determined (kex 1,330 ± 800 s-1, Δω 0.27 ± 0.1 ppm) (CHEY-J1, CHEY-r1)
regime: not stated by the authors. Table 2 prints per-residue 15N Δω from 0.27 ± 0.1 ppm (N94) to 9.4 ± 1 ppm (D64) at 600/700 MHz alongside local rates of 96 to 2,440 s-1, so no single regime applies; no minor-state peaks are reported (CHEY-r1).

structure_match.what: Mg-free wild-type crystal (Volz 1991 abstract: three sulfate ions, seven side chains in dual conformations; CHEY-r19). McDonald 2012 describes Y106 'out' and 'in' rotamers in this structure, cites the populated 'in' rotamer as support for rapid Y106 switching, and notes M85 in two conformations (CHEY-r1); the crystal gives no rate or population. A 1.08 Å apo structure (PDB ID not given in the rows) shows two β4–α4 loop conformations correlated with the Y106 rotamers, one interpreted as meta-active (CHEY-r27).

fallback_annotation: May have an alternate conformation differing at the active site and FliM-binding face (R18, R19, A36, D38, N62, D64, E67, L68, L69, T87, N94, V107, L127), based on 15N relaxation-compensated CPMG at 600 and 700 MHz (McDonald 2012, doi:10.1016/j.str.2012.05.008).
other_conditions: 10 mM Mg2+ (about 86% Mg-bound), 15 °C: possible by the same logic; the authors state CheY does not switch in a concerted two-state way 'whether Mg2+ is present or absent'. 11 residues, kex 246 ± 31 to 3,620 ± 460 s-1, pI 0.91–0.99 (CHEY-J4, CHEY-r2); A88 may carry a second, faster process (CHEY-J5).
1 mM and 75 mM Mg2+: two-point Rex only; V107 Rex about 28 s-1 at 1 mM, no rate (CHEY-J8, CHEY-r3, CHEY-r4).
BeFx + Mg2+ (phosphorylation mimic): possible. Small residual exchange redistributed toward the FliM interface, too few residues for rate fits (CHEY-J9, CHEY-r7).
caveats: The call is possible, not yes, because the data give per-residue local populations only and the authors argue against a single concerted inactive-active switch; linear shift trajectories across T87I, WT, A113P and BeFx states, which fit a two-state shift, are stated for Y106, V107 and E89 only. All NMR samples were in 50 mM sodium phosphate with no phosphate-free control, and the Mg-free crystal 3CHY has a sulfate next to N59 and K109 in the phosphorylation pocket.

protein: Human cyclophilin A (CypA), wild type
reference_state: Wild-type free CypA, 10 °C (also 0, 20, 25 °C); pH 6.5, 50 mM sodium phosphate, 1–2 mM DTT (2009: 2 mM)
literal_two_peak: does not: Authors: fast exchange limit for most amides, methyls intermediate; only 119–122, K91, H92, H126 and V128 reach the slow-exchange limit at 0/10 °C, with no population and no second peak set reported.
basis: At 10 °C free CypA exchanges on the µs–ms scale in an active-site/core network and in the 65–84 loop. A combined CPMG/R1rho fit gives one process with a 2.0 ± 0.1% excited state; methyl CPMG of residues in intermediate exchange gives a 5% minor state, and about 7% is an upper limit for the WT minor conformation overall.
kex: 10 °C: group I (active site/core) 1,140 ± 200 s-1 and group II (65–84 loop) 2,260 ± 200 s-1 (CYPA-J1, CYPA-J2, CYPA-r1); one global process 2,200 ± 90 s-1 (CYPA-J3, CYPA-r38). 20 °C: per-residue about 1,000–6,000 s-1 (CYPA-J22, CYPA-r12).
pB: 2.0 ± 0.1% (CYPA-r38); 5% from simultaneous fits of methyl residues in intermediate exchange (CYPA-r2); upper limit about 7% for the WT minor conformation overall, from amide kex and Rex (CYPA-r1); poorly determined in the deuterated per-residue fits (CYPA-J4)
regime: fast-to-intermediate for the 1,000–2,000 s-1 process: 'fast exchange limit for most resonances' with the chemical-shift difference 'not known' (2005), methyls in the 'intermediate time regime' (α < 1.5, 2005), most residues 'intermediate-fast exchange at all temperatures' (2009). Residues 119–122, K91, H92, H126 and V128 exchange on the 'intermediate-slow' timescale at 20 °C and are 'at the slow-exchange limit' at 10 and 0 °C only (2009); Table I gives only kA for residues 91, 92, 96, 119, 120 and 122, 0.85–2.74 s-1 at 10 °C and 0.54–1.85 s-1 at 0 °C (CYPA-J4, CYPA-J21; CYPA-r10, CYPA-r11).
residues: Group I: R55, S99, E120 amides and L39, I57, L98, A103 methyls (caption also lists 'Gly110'); group II: 65–84 loop (D66, F67, T68, N71, G74, K76, S77, K82 shown); 48 exchanging amides at 10 °C in deuterated data

structure_match.what: Room-temperature wild-type crystal with alternate side-chain rotamers for R55, M61, L98, S99 and F113. The rows tie the Ser99/Phe113 network to the millisecond group I process; crystal occupancies are not solution populations. The ID mapping (3K0N = WT, 3K0O = S99T) is taken from the 2024 paper (CYPA-r62).
S99T mutant crystal; the authors state the S99T major conformer recapitulates features of the WT minor conformer, which does not prove identical ensembles.

fallback_annotation: May have an alternate conformation differing in the 65–84 loop (D66, F67, T68, N71, G74, K76, S77, K82), based on 15N CPMG (doi:10.1038/nature04105) and combined CPMG/R1rho (doi:10.1039/c9sc04696h); fast-to-intermediate exchange, no second peak set observed. For the active-site side, a minor-state model is proposed from crystal alternates (3K0N/3K0O), not observed in solution.
other_conditions: Cyclosporin A-bound: possible. More than 98% major state, residual exchange in the 65–78 loop and near 108–110, no rate (CYPA-J6, CYPA-r4, CYPA-r37).

Substrate turnover (Suc-AFPF-pNA or FGP peptide): possible. kex 2,730 ± 220 s-1 at 10 °C or about 1,500 s-1, no population; binding and release alone can produce dispersion (CYPA-J7, CYPA-J8, CYPA-J9, CYPA-r3, CYPA-r35, CYPA-r36).
S99T mutant, 10 °C: yes. CEST kex 188.3 ± 9.5 s-1, pB 1.22 ± 0.03% (CYPA-J10, CYPA-r22).
S99T rescue mutants: yes, with a second minor state (pB 1.93 / 4.32%, pC 0.31 / 0.73%) (CYPA-J11, CYPA-r23, CYPA-r24).
D66A mutant: yes, near the detection threshold. kex 2,000 ± 350 s-1, pB 0.5 ± 0.1%; the authors say D66A stabilizes a conformation resembling the WT excited state (CYPA-J12, CYPA-r39).
Cryogenic crystals (180 K and below): most network alternates disappear, a crystal temperature effect (CYPA-J18).
caveats: The number of apo processes is disputed: two collective groups (r1), one global process (r38), or a continuum of per-residue rates (r10–r12). All apo NMR checked in the cached text was recorded in 50 mM sodium phosphate with no phosphate-free control. MD places Phe113 rotamer exchange at nanoseconds to microseconds, which leaves its assignment to the millisecond process open.

protein: Human HtrA2 PDZ domain, isolated (author residues 349–458)
reference_state: Isolated wild-type apo HtrA2 PDZ, 298 K and 283 K; PBS pH 7.4 (the PDZ sample buffer; the NMR buffer is not stated separately), no added divalent metal; 500 µM
literal_two_peak: cannot tell: No regime statement and no Δω printed; the authors report no minor-state peaks.
basis: The isolated apo PDZ shows µs–ms exchange in the N-terminus, helix α5 with its loop to β15, and helix α7 with its preceding loop, fitted globally as one two-site process with a 15.2% minor state at 298 K. Methyl MQ CPMG gives a similar 16.6% minor state, which the authors call 'indicative of the same underlying process'. SEC-MALS gives a dimerization KD lower limit of 13 ± 1.65 mM; the authors do not link dimerization to the CPMG minor state.
kex: reported as τex, not kex: 0.42 ± 0.004 ms at 298 K and 0.98 ± 0.005 ms at 283 K (fit errors from a single experiment, n = 1); kex ≈ 1/τex is the row's assumption, giving about 2,400 s-1 (HTPDZ-J1) and about 1,020 s-1 (HTPDZ-J28); methyl τex 1.19 ± 0.07 ms at 298 K (HTPDZ-J3)
pB: 15.2% at 298 K (HTPDZ-r1); 16.1% at 283 K (HTPDZ-r2); the text says only 'decreasing from 16.1 to 15.2%', with no error given and the temperature assignment from Fig. 2c; methyl 16.6 ± 0.4% at 298 K (HTPDZ-r3)
regime: not stated by the authors; no Δω printed. The 2 kHz spin-lock control gives mainly planar R2(R1ρ), so no faster (< 80 µs) contribution is seen; this is not a regime assignment (HTPDZ-J4).
residues: N-terminus, helix α5 and the α5–β15 loop, helix α7 and its preceding loop; at 283 K also the β17–β18 loop. Per-residue ΔR2eff places exchange on 30 residues at 298 K and 35 at 283 K (30 passing plus 5 exchange-broadened) by the row's transcription rule (ΔR2eff ≥ 2 s-1; the authors give no threshold) (HTPDZ-J1, HTPDZ-J28); the residues entering the global fit are not listed
fallback_annotation: May have an alternate conformation differing at the N-terminus, helix α5 and the α5–β15 loop, and helix α7 with its preceding loop, based on 15N BEST-TROSY CPMG at 298 and 283 K and methyl MQ CPMG (doi:10.1038/s41467-024-48997-5).
other_conditions: Peptide-bound isolated PDZ: unknown, not measured in the rows (HTPDZ-J8).
Isolated PDZ with Ca2+ or Zn2+: unknown; methyl CPMG exists in the source but has no evidence row (HTPDZ-J9).
Full-length S306A trimer, 313 K, apo: exchange in helix α5 among other regions, two-point data only, mutant construct (HTPDZ-J11, HTPDZ-r10).

Full-length trimer, 40 °C: a PDZ hexamer-interface contribution and interface exchange when neighbours are held open; oligomerization, not intradomain exchange (HTPDZ-J12, HTPDZ-J13, HTPDZ-r14, HTPDZ-r15).
caveats: The minor state is not identified structurally. Backbone and methyl lifetimes at 298 K differ about three-fold in samples prepared differently ([U-15N,13C] backbone sample versus [U-2H] methyl-labelled sample in 99.9% D2O), although the authors call the two data sets 'indicative of the same underlying process'. All isolated-PDZ NMR was in PBS with no phosphate-free control, and the exchanging loops are where divalent cations bind.

protein: Human K-Ras4B G-domain (residues 1–169), wild type
reference_state: Wild-type K-Ras4B 1–169 with native GTP and Mg2+, no partner; 298 K, pH 7.0, 20 mM HEPES, 5 mM MgCl2 (GDP·Mg is listed under other_conditions)
literal_two_peak: qualifies: Authors: 'moderately slow', 'intermediate-to-slow' (|Δω|/kex > 0.5); a second CEST dip for state 1 is seen in WT GTP·Mg at 298 K, and 31P γ1/γ2 are separate peaks at 278 K in a C118S background; no HSQC peak doubling for WT at 298 K is reported.
basis: Free GTP·Mg K-Ras exchanges between a dominant state 2 and a GDP-like, partly disordered state 1 across Switch I, Switch II and the P-loop, with kex about 400 s-1 and 8–10% state 1 in two HEPES laboratories and in PBS/EDTA. In 31P spectra of a C118S-background protein the two states give separate γ-phosphate peaks.
kex: 400 ± 12 s-1 (KRAS-J1, KRAS-r1); 414 ± 3 s-1 (KRAS-J2, KRAS-r26); 404 ± 54 s-1 in PBS/EDTA (KRAS-J3, KRAS-r17)
pB: state 1: 10.15 ± 0.47% (KRAS-r1); 9.6 ± 0.1% (KRAS-r26); 7.8 ± 0.2% higher-energy state (pE) in PBS/EDTA, read as state 1 by the entry (KRAS-r17)
regime: Authors: exchange 'proceeded at a moderately slow rate', and residues entering the global fit are in the 'intermediate-to-slow regime with values of |Δω|/kex > 0.5' (KRAS-J1, KRAS-r1). 15N CEST shows a second dip for state 1 directly in WT GTP·Mg at 298 K (e.g. T35, E62; KRAS-r1). 31P: γ1 (state 1) and γ2 (state 2) resonances are separate peaks in C118S-background K-Ras·GTP at 278 K, with no rate (KRAS-J25, KRAS-r38). Per-residue 15N |Δϖ| are plotted (Fig. 3a, dashed line at 0.5 ppm) but not printed in the cached text.
residues: Switch I, Switch II and the P-loop; 45 residues with fitted |Δϖ| > 0.5 ppm (Source Data Fig. 3); T35, I36, E62, Y71 shown (KRAS-r1)
fallback_annotation: May have an alternate conformation differing at Switch I, Switch II and the P-loop (a GDP-like state 1 with a random-coil-like Switch I), based on joint 15N CPMG, 1HN CPMG and 15N CEST (Hansen 2023, doi:10.1038/s41594-023-01070-z).
other_conditions: GDP·Mg in HEPES without EDTA, 298 K: no_evidence. No significantly populated millisecond state by 15N CEST on ten Switch I/II residues (KRAS-J6, KRAS-r10).
GDP·Mg methyls, 25 °C: possible. Methyl CPMG flat, but adiabatic dispersion detects faster effector-lobe exchange at I36 and I55 (KRAS-J7, KRAS-r83).

GDP·Mg in PBS with 10 mM EDTA: minor state 2.8 ± 0.2% (CPMG kex 164 ± 28 s-1) or 3.8 ± 0.1% (CEST kex 267 ± 20 s-1) with Mg2+-free-like shifts, which the authors read as a pre-formed Mg2+-free-like state; the entry suspects an EDTA versus Mg artefact (KRAS-J4, KRAS-J5, KRAS-r13, KRAS-r21).
GTP·Mg + B-Raf RBD (equimolar): no_evidence; RBD quenches the exchange (KRAS-J12).
GTP·Mg mutants G12C, G12D, Q61R: yes. Same process with lower state 1 (G12C 6.97 ± 0.17%, G12D 9.00 ± 0.44%, Q61R 1.8%) (KRAS-J14, KRAS-J20, KRAS-r2, KRAS-r3, KRAS-r27).
caveats: Ras has no nucleotide-free apo form, so the call depends on the nucleotide: yes for GTP·Mg, no_evidence for GDP·Mg in HEPES. The 31P two-peak observation is in a C118S background, not WT. No structure of WT state 1 with native GTP is solved (GDP-like shifts and random-coil-like Switch I only); open-Switch-I crystals exist only for mutants or analogue-bound protein, and state-1 mutants T35S and V29G show extra or faster processes, so state 1 may be heterogeneous. GMPPNP raises state 1, so analogue-loaded samples cannot stand in for native GTP.

protein: Bovine pancreatic ribonuclease A (RNase A), wild type
reference_state: Wild-type free RNase A, 293 K (RelaxDB label condition; also 283 and 298 K). Beach 2005: pH 6.3, 20 mM perdeuterated MES, 10 mM NaCl, 600 µM. Cluster fits (Khirich 2015): 5 mM MES, 7 mM NaCl, pH 6.4. Buffer-study reference: 5 mM MES, 400 µM.
literal_two_peak: does not: Global and cluster motions are fast (buffer study: 'nearly all ... in the fast limit'); only R33 is slow, and 'no minor peak could be detected'.
basis: Free RNase A shows µs–ms exchange that one global two-state fit per temperature describes, with a 90–93% major state. Later cluster fits split it into a loop 1/β1/β4 network around His48, loop 4 near His119, and Arg33 as a separate process, each with its own rate and population.
kex: global 1,080 ± 80 / 1,390 ± 70 / 1,750 ± 130 s-1 at 283 / 293 / 298 K (RNASE-J1, RNASE-r1–r3); His48 cluster 2,650 s-1 at 25 °C, pH 6.4 (RNASE-J5, RNASE-r18); loop 4 1,610 s-1 at 25 °C, pooled pH 5.5–7.0 (RNASE-J6, RNASE-r19); R33 1,215 s-1 at 25 °C (RNASE-J7, RNASE-r68)
pB: reported as pA, so pB = 1 − pA: global fits pA 90–93% across 283–298 K (pB 7–10%), which Beach says reflects 'uncertainty in fitting for pa' (RNASE-J1); His48 cluster reported as pA = 92.5 ± 0.7% at pH 6.4 (pB 7.5 ± 0.7%; the ± is the spread of an average over temperature) (RNASE-J5); loop 4 reported as pA = 95.9 ± 0.9% at 25 °C (pB 4.1 ± 0.9%; the ± is the standard deviation over pH) (RNASE-J6); R33 reported as pA = 99.5% (pB 0.5%) (RNASE-J7, RNASE-r68); pA:pB 0.95:0.05 in the proton-inventory study (RNASE-J3, RNASE-r24)
regime: Beach 2005: no regime stated; the minor resonance is called 'invisible'. Buffer study: dispersion fit with the fast-exchange equation, 'nearly all of the MES-reference motions are in the fast limit' (RNASE-J9, RNASE-r10). Proton-inventory study, WT 298 K: Δω 510 s-1 (F46) and 356 s-1 (T100) with kex 1,657 s-1 (RNASE-J3, RNASE-r24). Cluster R1ρ data were 'assumed to be in fast exchange'; at pH 4.5 the His48 cluster leaves the CPMG window (13,400 s-1 by R1ρ at 25 °C on a deuterated sample, RNASE-J5). Only R33 is called slow: 'slow-exchange characteristics (kex/Δω ~ 0.75 at 500 MHz)', Δω 5.41 ± 0.30 ppm, and 'no minor peak could be detected' (RNASE-J7, RNASE-r68).
residues: Global fit at 293 K: Q11, S15, S16, T17, N44, F46, A64, K66, N71, D83, T100, Q101, H119 (43 residues pass the Rex screen); His48 cluster S15, S16, T17, F46, T82, D83, Q101; loop 4 A64, K66, T70, N71; R33

structure_match.what: pTppAp-bound crystal (the authors' own complex). Beach 2005 compares it crystal-to-crystal with apo 7RSA (backbone RMSD 0.69 Å) and describes an equilibrium between 'open and closed enzyme forms'. The minor state's resemblance to the bound form rests on 15N Δω sign agreement (17 of 20 residues); its structure is not determined.
Apo crystal structure, the apo comparison structure in the same analysis; 'apo-like/open comparison state' is the entry's gloss.

fallback_annotation: May have an alternate, ligand-bound-like conformation differing at loop 1/β1/β4 around His48 (S15, S16, T17, F46, T82, D83, Q101) and at loop 4 (A64, K66, T70, N71), based on 15N relaxation-compensated CPMG (Beach 2005, doi:10.1021/ja0514949; cluster fits doi:10.1021/acs.jpcb.5b00212).
other_conditions: pTppAp-bound (substrate mimic): yes. kex 1,316 ± 160 to 1,920 ± 250 s-1, major state 90–96% (RNASE-J16, RNASE-r4–r6).
5'-AMP or 3'-UMP bound: possible. Exchange reshaped (loop 4 687 ± 41 s-1 with 5'-AMP), no population (RNASE-J17, RNASE-s19, RNASE-s21).

pH 4.5, 25 °C: the His48 cluster exchanges at 13,400 s-1 by R1rho on a deuterated sample, fitted assuming fast exchange, too fast for CPMG; loop 4 still disperses at 2,080 ± 340 s-1 (RNASE-J5, RNASE-J6, RNASE-r15, RNASE-r16).
Heavy water: the His48 group slows (isotope effect 2.2 ± 0.3), loop 4 does not (RNASE-J3, RNASE-J4).
100 mM phosphate, 80 mM sulfate or 100 mM acetate: artefact suspected; anions change residue-specific dispersion (RNASE-J19).
His48-network mutants: T17A and H48C-4MI keep exchange; H48C, H48G, T82A and the loop-1 chimera lose it there (RNASE-J23).
caveats: Whether this is one collective motion or several (His48 network, loop 4, R33) is disputed between papers, and 'cluster 1' means different regions in different papers. Free-WT samples were in MES (later also 1% DSS); the only buffer control is a stated, unshown MES-versus-unbuffered comparison. Of the 43 residues behind the RelaxDB labels, only 13 entered the 293 K global fit.

protein: Human VHR (Vaccinia H1-related) phosphatase, full-length wild type
reference_state: Wild-type apo VHR, 25 °C; pH 6.5, 20 mM Bis-Tris propane, 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM TCEP, 1 mM EDTA, no phosphate added; CPMG sample 700 µM 2H/15N (Hahn-echo 700 or 965 µM)
literal_two_peak: cannot tell: regime not stated by the authors; the 1.2% minor state is seen only through dispersion and no second peak set is reported.
basis: At 25 °C nine amides in the variable insert and the acid loop fit one shared process with a minor state of about 1.2% (reported as pA = 98.8 ± 0.1%). CPMG |ΔωN| is several-fold larger than the apo-to-tungstate shift (e.g. A63 930 vs 260 s-1), and the authors say the interconverting structures 'remain unclear'.
kex: 1,530 ± 200 s-1, combined variable-insert + acid-loop fit, proposed by the authors as one concerted process on F-test grounds (p = 8.2 × 10−14) (VHR-J1, VHR-r1); the separate fits remain valid and give acid loop 1,400 ± 200 s-1 and variable insert 2,100 ± 460 s-1
pB: reported as pA = 98.8 ± 0.1% in the combined fit, so pB = 1.2 ± 0.1%; separate fits reported as pA = 98.9 ± 0.1% (acid loop, pB 1.1 ± 0.1%) and pA = 98.5 ± 0.4% (variable insert, pB 1.5 ± 0.4%) (VHR-r1)
residues: Variable insert A63, R66, N72; acid loop K89, D92, E95, F96, L98, S99; Hahn-echo adds R36, Y78, R119, C124, G161, D164
fallback_annotation: May have an alternate conformation differing at the variable insert (A63, R66, N72) and the acid loop (K89, D92, E95, F96, L98, S99), based on 15N relaxation-compensated CPMG at 600, 700 and 800 MHz (doi:10.1021/acs.biochem.0c00245).
other_conditions: Tungstate-bound WT: possible. Hahn-echo exchange profile similar to apo, no rate (VHR-J3, VHR-r3).
N74A mutant, apo and tungstate-bound: most variable-insert and acid-loop residues 'remain exchange broadened', read by the authors as retained or enhanced ms motion, no rate (VHR-J4, VHR-J5).
Apo crystals 8TK6 and 9DJ9 at 100 K: no_evidence; they are superposed in SI Fig. S6 with no author comment on loop differences, which cannot exclude a 1.2% solution state (VHR-J8, VHR-r10, VHR-r11).

Fragment F17 complex (8TK2): the variable-insert E-loop A63–N72 shifts by up to 1.4 Å, which the authors attribute to F17 binding ('likely to accommodate F17 binding'); not the CPMG minor state (VHR-J9, VHR-r9).
caveats: Single temperature and one study. The coupling of the two loops rests on the authors' model choice (combined versus separate fits). The dissertation that RelaxDB cites as the data source was not read, so its equivalence to the 2020 data is unverified.

protein: Salmonella typhimurium NtrC N-terminal receiver domain (124 residues), wild type
reference_state: Wild-type unphosphorylated (apo) isolated receiver domain, 25 °C (298 K), pH 6.75, 50 mM sodium phosphate, 10% D2O, 0.75 mM; Mg2+ not stated; no phosphate-free control
literal_two_peak: does not: The activation exchange is too fast to be suppressed by 1000 Hz CPMG and the methyl data are fitted with a fast-exchange model; the 14% active state is seen through dispersion and the D88 shift position, and no second peak set is reported.
basis: The unphosphorylated wild-type domain switches between inactive and active conformations. 15N CPMG combined with independently measured exchange-free R2 gives the rate, and the D88 chemical-shift ruler combined with the dispersion fit puts 14% of molecules in the active state. Methyl 1H CPMG at 18 switch-interface residues gives a similar rate, but with the population fixed at 14% rather than fitted.
kex: 13,580 ± 850 s-1 (kIA 1,900 ± 125 s-1, kAI 11,600 ± 775 s-1), 15N backbone, global two-state fit (NTRC-J1, NTRC-r20); 15,458 ± 452 s-1, methyl 1H, fast-exchange model (NTRC-J2, NTRC-r7, NTRC-r9)
pB: 14% active (the minor state), from the D88 chemical-shift ruler combined with the dispersion fit, not from dispersion alone (NTRC-J1, NTRC-r20). The methyl fit imposes the same 14% and is not an independent population (NTRC-J2, NTRC-r7).
regime: Fast. The protein summary records that this exchange is too fast to be suppressed by 1000 Hz CPMG (JMB 2014), so the rate rests on dispersion plus exchange-free R2 (NTRC-J1, NTRC-J19); the methyl fit uses a fast-exchange model (NTRC-J2). No Δω is printed in the rows.
residues: Helix 4 / switch region. Population ruler D88; the residues in the 15N global fit are shown only by colour, and the shared Fig. 2 legend (D11, Q68, I69, K70, Q71, R72, V78, T82, H84, L87, D88, A89, V91, Y94, F99, D100, Y101, L102) is not allocated per sample (NTRC-J1). Methyl probes V9, V18, L19, L40, L43, V50, L66, L76, V78, I79, I80, A83, L87, A90, V91, A93, L102, L114; I55-γ2 fits poorly and is excluded (NTRC-J2, NTRC-J3).

structure_match.what: BeF3−-activated NMR ensemble at 35 °C. Compared with the apo 2MSL ensemble, helix α4 rotates and Y94 contacts to helix 3 are replaced by Q96 contacts. An activation-mimic endpoint, not a structure fitted to the 14% minor state.
Phosphorylated receiver structure, compared with inactive 1DC7: helix-4 register shift and rotation that exposes a hydrophobic surface. Read as abstract only; no rate.
BeF3−-activated RDC-assisted structures showing the same register shift and a correlated T82/Y101 change as the phosphorylated form. Abstract only.

fallback_annotation: May have an alternate (active-like) conformation differing at helix 4 and the switch region, based on 15N TROSY CPMG and methyl 1H CPMG relaxation dispersion of the unphosphorylated domain (doi:10.1016/j.cell.2009.11.022; doi:10.1021/ja107410x).
other_conditions: BeF3−-bound WT (phosphorylation mimic), same buffer, 25 °C: yes. kex about 1,950 s-1 (1,940 ± 290 in 2009; 1,950 ± 290 or ± 200 in 2014), with the active state at ≥ 99.4% (pA ≥ 0.994), so the inactive minor state is ≤ 0.6% (converted) (NTRC-J18, NTRC-r23, NTRC-r14). A second, faster process around Y101 has a rough kex of about 30,000 ± 12,000 (unit implied s-1), population not separable (NTRC-J19, NTRC-r14).

D86N: yes. kex 16,450 ± 840 s-1 with 43% active (NTRC-J24, NTRC-r21). D86N/A89T: yes. kex 20,050 ± 1080 s-1 with 65% active, so the inactive state is the minor one at 35% (converted) (NTRC-J25, NTRC-r22).

Hydrogen-bond mutants: possible. S85D 2,900 ± 200, S85G 3,200 ± 900, Y101F 3,300 ± 800, Q96N 3,800 ± 600, S85D/Y101F 2,800 ± 700 s-1, no population; S85N restores 16,900 ± 1,900 s-1 (NTRC-J26 to NTRC-J31, NTRC-r24 to NTRC-r29).

Y101L: possible. kex 2,200 ± 300 s-1 at 18 listed residues (NTRC-J34, NTRC-r15); the faster Y101-linked process is absent except at S13, where sodium binding is suspected (NTRC-J35, NTRC-J36). BeF3−-bound Y101L 1,500 ± 600 s-1 (NTRC-J37, NTRC-r18).
Phosphorylated WT: unknown. The 2001 abstract says phosphorylation shifts the equilibrium toward the active state, with no rate or residues (NTRC-J14, NTRC-r5).
caveats: All Kern-lab NMR samples use 50 mM sodium phosphate for a phosphorylatable domain with no phosphate-free control, and the authors suspect sodium binding at S13 (NTRC-J36); the NMR collaborator is asked whether to flag the 14% and kex as buffer-dependent. The population rests on one ruler residue (D88) combined with dispersion. The minor state is called active from its shifts; no structure was fitted to it, and the activated structures are BeF3− or phosphorylated endpoints, two of them read as abstracts. MD macrostate populations (about 52% and 48%, not assigned to active or inactive; NTRC-J6, NTRC-r1) were not used. The RelaxDB R1/R2/NOE sample (2001 study, abstract only) is unidentified.

protein: Third IgG-binding domain of streptococcal protein G (GB3), 56 residues, entry sequence with Q2
reference_state: Wild-type protonated free GB3 in isotropic solution: 24 °C, pH 5.8, 30 mM phosphate, 9% D2O, 1.8 mM (Hall and Fushman 2003, matching the BMRB 5839 conditions); 25 °C, pH 7.0, 50 mM sodium phosphate, 50 mM NaCl, 4 mM for multiple-quantum relaxation; 25 °C, pH 6.3 for the four-field broadening limit
literal_two_peak: cannot tell: No regime is stated for the room-temperature wild-type processes and no second peak set is reported; the only stated regime is fast exchange, in perdeuterated GB3 at 262–275 K.
basis: Room-temperature amide 15N relaxation of protonated wild-type GB3 is nearly silent. V39 is the one amide that needs an exchange term at all five fields and in every tumbling model; the helix Rex is an anisotropic-tumbling artefact, and relaxation-compensated CPMG finds no dispersion up to about 8 ms. Multiple-quantum relaxation detects slow correlated shift fluctuations (Cα–Cβ at 17 residues, C'–N over most of the backbone) with rate ranges but no population or minor state. Microsecond exchange with measured lifetimes appears only in perdeuterated GB3 below room temperature.
kex: V39: not fitted; Rex 0.78, 0.51 and 0.28 s-1 under the isotropic, axially symmetric and fully anisotropic models (GB3-J44, GB3-5839_20261017120337-r3; five fields, GB3-J13, GB3-r3). Multiple-quantum ranges, not per-residue fits: Cα–Cβ typical 100–160 s-1 (GB3-J9, GB3-5839_20261015212628-r4); C'–N bounded at about 110–200 to 430 s-1 (GB3-J10, GB3-5839_20261015212628-r2).
pB: not measured in the reference state (GB3-J9, GB3-J10, GB3-J13, GB3-J44)
regime: Not stated for the room-temperature processes. The C'–N authors note this motion would give 15N single-quantum Rex under 0.3 s-1 and require Δω_N < 0.18 Δω_C' (GB3-J10). Backbone 15N exchange broadening is about 0.15 s-1 or less at 900 MHz, 25 °C, pH 6.3 (GB3-J14, GB3-r26). Fast exchange is stated only for perdeuterated GB3 at 262–275 K (GB3-J47, GB3-J50).
residues: V39 in the helix–β3 loop (GB3-J13, GB3-J44); K13, G9 and T49 are unconfirmed candidates (GB3-J45). Cα–Cβ: V39, V54, L5, A20, Y3, A23, with clustered contributions at K4, N8, T11, V21, D22, E27, K28, Q32, D36, D46, K50 (GB3-J9). C'–N: most residues, discussed as Y3–E15, A20–D40 and G41–T55 (GB3-J10).
fallback_annotation: May have slow, low-amplitude conformational exchange at V39 in the helix–β3 loop and slow correlated backbone shift fluctuations, based on multi-field 15N relaxation and 13C multiple-quantum relaxation of protonated GB3 (doi:10.1023/a:1025467918856; doi:10.1021/ja060406x; doi:10.1007/s10858-018-0205-2); microsecond motion of the first β-turn G9–K13 was measured only in perdeuterated GB3 below room temperature (doi:10.1002/anie.201603501).
other_conditions: Perdeuterated GB3, 262–275 K, pH 6.5, 50 mM sodium phosphate, 100 mM NaCl: possible. First-turn amide 1H R1rho, G9–K13 share τex 35.9 ± 1.3 µs (262 K) to 9.1 ± 0.4 µs (275 K), fast exchange, population not separable (GB3-J47, GB3-5839_20261017120337-r5 to GB3-5839_20261017120337-r8); individual fits 7.1–16 µs at K10, L12, K13 at 275 K (GB3-J51, GB3-5839_20261017120337-r18). Backbone 15N profiles are flat (GB3-J48).

Perdeuterated GB3 with 13CHD2 ILV methyls, 275 K: possible. Seven methyl carbons exchange with τex 11–58 µs (GB3 average 27 µs), the methyl proton only at V54 γ2 (13 ± 0.88 µs); population not separable, and the rotamer fractions are model populations (GB3-J50, GB3-5839_20261017120337-r16, GB3-5839_20261017120337-r17, GB3-5839_20261017120337-r19).
Extrapolation to 310 K, not a measurement: first-turn τex 371 ± 115 ns (Arrhenius) or 409 ± 126 ns (Eyring) (GB3-J19, GB3-5839_20261017120337-r9, GB3-r20).
T11K/K19E/V42E mutant, deuterated amides, 283 versus 298 K: possible. Extra R1rho at N8, T16, T17, N37 and T53 that shrinks on warming; no dispersion, rate or population (GB3-J17, GB3-r9).
E27Q mutant, 298 K, amide H/D exchange: β2 amides exchange within the 0.5 h dead time and β1 partners over hours; solvent-exchange constants, not opening rates (GB3-J41, GB3-r46, GB3-r47).
caveats: The BMRB 5839 deposition screen flags V39 by R2/R1, and its helix flags (K28, K31, Q32, D36) fit the anisotropic tumbling the 2003 paper identified; the screen does not set the call. The Cα–Cβ rate uses perdeuterated GB3 as an approximate CSA baseline, so baseline and rate are coupled. The V39 Rex depends on the tumbling model, and the pH 6.3 four-field study does not say whether V39 is an exception. Crystal alternate side-chain conformers (1IGD/2IGD) and RDC rotamer populations describe side-chain heterogeneity, not a minor backbone state, so no structure is matched (GB3-J28, GB3-J31). the NMR collaborator is asked whether the perdeuterated cold-sample exchange should count toward the WT apo answer.

protein: Cupriavidus metallidurans CH34 SilB C-terminal domain (SilB 440–521), isolated
reference_state: Free wild-type isolated SilB C-terminal domain (SilB440-521, the entry sequence, six-His tag cleaved), no added metal. The RelaxDB source sample (doi:10.1021/bi200005k, now full text): 1.0 mM uniformly 15N-labelled protein, 25 °C, pH 6.0, 50 mM MES, 600 MHz, single field, R2 from an R1rho decay (SILB-J1, J2, J9 marked is_wt_apo). The Ag+- and Cu+-bound samples of the same paper are other sample states.
literal_two_peak: cannot tell: the source states no exchange regime, prints no kex, population or Delta-omega and shows no second peak set for the apo domain; it speaks of slow motions of the metal-binding loop and states that the apo protein does not simply exchange with a conformation close to the metal-bound state (SILB-J2, J4; E-r1, E-r2). Without kex and Delta-omega the E-033 computation cannot be made. The one peak that does disappear, the Met65 methyl in the Ag+-bound sample, is a bound-state observation presumed to be line broadening (SILB-J7).
basis: Reference state: in the RelaxDB source sample (apo domain, 25 °C, pH 6.0, 600 MHz) the text names His22, Ala24, Gln29, 'Ala31', Met33 and Met35 as the residues with increased R1rho-derived R2 (Figure 6B: about 11, 15 and 12.5 s-1 at His22, Gln29 and Met35 against a baseline near 8-9 s-1), and the Tensor2 model-free fit returns exchange terms only in the metal-binding loop, at Ala24 (about 1.6 s-1), Gln29 (6.0), Gly31 (2.6), Ala32 (1.5), Met33 (3.3) and Met35 (4.3) in Figure S6C; His22 is fitted with S2 near 1.0 and no exchange term (SILB-J2, E-r1). Under the single-field Rex rule of 2026-10-20 this is exchange detected in the reference state without a population, so the call is 'possible'. The rest of the domain is rigid: S2 above 0.8 for most of the 63 fitted residues, tau_i about 70 ps, lower S2 only at the N terminus and in the loops between strands 3 and 4 and between 4 and 5, and no exchange term outside the loop (SILB-J1, J9). Adding one equivalent of Ag+ removes the excess transverse relaxation while leaving tumbling and fast motion unchanged, and the authors state that the apo protein does not simply exchange with a conformation close to the metal-bound state (SILB-J4, E-r2).
kex: not reported: Rex only, read from Figure S6C as about 1.5-6.0 s-1 at six residues, from a single-field R1rho-based fit (SILB-J2)
pB: not reported (SILB-J2); no population is fitted for the apo or the Ag+-bound sample
regime: Not stated. No Delta-omega is printed and no kex is fitted, so no regime can be computed; the authors call the loop motion slow relative to tumbling (tau_c 6.28 ns isotropic, axially anisotropic tensor preferred) and describe the micro- to millisecond window qualitatively (SILB-J2).
residues: Metal-binding loop. Increased apo R2 (Figure 6B, text p. 2200): His22, Ala24, Gln29, 'Ala31' (the sequence has Gly31 and Ala32), Met33, Met35. Fitted Rex (Figure S6C): Ala24, Gln29, Gly31, Ala32, Met33, Met35; none at His22. Entry numbering equals the article numbering (SILB-J2). Exchange is absent elsewhere in the apo domain (SILB-J9) and at these same residues once Ag+ is bound (SILB-J4). ps-ns mobility: N terminus and the surface loops between strands 3 and 4 and between 4 and 5, not enumerated (SILB-J1).

other_conditions: Apo domain, 25 °C, pH 6.0, 50 mM MES, 1.0 mM, 600 MHz single field (2011 RelaxDB source, full text): possible. Exchange confined to the metal-binding loop; S2 above 0.8 elsewhere, tau_i about 70 ps (SILB-J1, J2, J9; E-r1).

Ag+-bound domain (1 equivalent of AgNO3), same buffer and temperature: no detectable loop exchange; R2 of the loop residues falls to the 8-9 s-1 baseline while tumbling and fast motion are unchanged (SILB-J4, E-r2).
Ag+-bound domain, methyl region: the Met65 1H-13C correlation is broadened below the detection limit, presumed line broadening, process unidentified (SILB-J7, SILB-r3).
Apo E. coli CusF (1ZEQ) compared with apo SilB440-521: same OB fold, backbone rmsd 1.17 A over 264 atoms; a homolog, not a second state (SILB-J8, SILB-r4).

Different construct (N-terminal plus membrane-proximal domains, 2016): unknown. The abstract names no probe, motion or timescale; the finding that the C-terminal site fills first during Ag+ titration is binding, not motion (SILB-J5, J6; SILB-r2).
caveats: Call raised from unknown to possible on 2026-10-20 after the RelaxDB source paper (doi:10.1021/bi200005k) was read in full: exchange is detected in the reference state as single-field model-free Rex in the metal-binding loop, and under the single-field Rex rule decided that night (ledger/redraft_notes.json, _RULE_single_field_rex) author-reported Rex in the reference state counts as exchange detected without a population. Fixed caveat: single-field Rex can also come from anisotropic tumbling; a dispersion experiment would confirm. That caveat bites harder here than usual, because the preferred diffusion model is axially anisotropic; on the other hand R2 came from an R1rho decay chosen to suppress exchange, which makes the surviving loop terms harder to explain away. All Rex and S2 values are read from Supporting Information Figure S6, a plot; the text gives no table. The text prints 'Ala31' where the sequence has Gly31 and Ala32, so both positions are kept. Thr34 was not fitted and overlapping resonances were excluded (63 apo, 57 Ag+-bound residues). The abstract-only row SILB-r1 is superseded and no longer cited; the 2016 paper on the other construct remains an abstract. Both readers passed all four rows with no flags (ledger/sr_dual/S6_r6_17266_20261020221901_flags.json); the PDF adjudication is in ledger/adjudication_pdf_batch2.json.

protein: Vibrio cholerae peptidyl-tRNA hydrolase (VcPth), full length with His tag (pET-NH6)
reference_state: Wild-type apo (no substrate), 298 K, pH 6.5, 20 mM NaH2PO4, 50 mM NaCl, 1 mM DTT, 0.1% NaN3, 0.5 mM 15N; 700 MHz, single field
literal_two_peak: does not: The only stated regime is the authors' reading of the missing N118 amide as intermediate exchange; no dispersion was recorded and no second peak set is reported.
basis: Single-field model-free fits need exchange terms at T22, A79, G115–H117, D147 and H192, and the N118 and K146 amides are missing in the wild type but N118 returns in active-site mutants. The judgments leave both unresolved: single-field Rex cannot be separated from anisotropic tumbling, and a missing peak gives no rate. Under the single-field Rex rule of 2026-10-20 (author-reported Rex in the reference state from a full-text relaxation analysis counts as exchange detected without a population) the call is 'possible'; no new evidence was added. No relaxation-dispersion study was found, but the dispersion queries used E. coli Pth terms, so this is a search gap.
kex: not measured (VCPTH-J3, VCPTH-J12)
pB: not measured (VCPTH-J3, VCPTH-J4)
regime: Not measured. The authors read the missing N118 amide as intermediate exchange from transient N118–H24 contact; solvent exchange was argued against, not tested (VCPTH-J4, VCPTH-r4). At pH 6.0 and below (visible on lowering from 6.5 to 6.0; assigned at pH 5.2) the N118 peak returns, which fits either H24 protonation or slower base-catalysed solvent exchange (VCPTH-J5, VCPTH-r5).
residues: Rex at T22 (next to catalytic H24), A79, base loop G115–H117 at the helix α3 N-terminus, lid D147 and H192 in the C-terminal hairpin (VCPTH-J3); missing amides N118 (helix α3 N-cap) and K146 (lid flap) (VCPTH-J4).

D97N and N118D mutant crystals in which H24 hydrogen-bonds N118/D118, the other half of the proposed switch. Static mutant structures, no rate.

fallback_annotation: May have slow motion near the catalytic H24, at the helix α3 N-cap and in the lid, based on single-field 15N relaxation and missing amide peaks of the free enzyme (doi:10.1261/rna.057620.116); no dispersion data exist.
other_conditions: H24N: unknown. The single-field exchange term moves from the H24 region to the lid hinge G139 and L154; no rate (VCPTH-J7, VCPTH-r2).
N118D: unknown. Larger slow-motion terms near H24, residues figure-only, no rate (VCPTH-J8, VCPTH-r3).
E. coli Pth homolog crystals: the lid loop–helix α4 has high B-factors and differs between free 2PTH and tRNA-fragment-bound 3VJR, which may reflect packing (VCPTH-J11, VCPTH-r8).
caveats: Call changed from unknown to possible on 2026-10-20 by the single-field Rex rule (ledger/redraft_notes.json, _RULE_single_field_rex), not by new evidence: the judgments (VCPTH-J3, J4) stay unresolved, and the only us-ms evidence is still the single-field model-free Rex and the missing N118/K146 amides of the 2017 paper. The input card pairs the V. cholerae sequence and 2MJL with UniProt P0A7D1 (E. coli Pth); V. cholerae Pth is treated as the entry. All VcPth NMR uses phosphate, which could occupy the basic 5'-phosphate clamp, with no control. One 2017 paper supplies every VcPth row.

protein: Escherichia coli RfaH C-terminal domain (entry native 111–162), studied as the isolated domain (native 101–162 or 102–162)
reference_state: Wild-type isolated CTD (β-barrel), no partner, 25 °C, pH 6.5: perdeuterated 1.0 mM U-[15N/2H] sample in 25 mM potassium phosphate, 0.5 mM EDTA, 1 mM PMSF (PNAS 2025); protonated 0.7–1 mM 15N sample in 20 mM sodium phosphate, 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA (eLife)
literal_two_peak: qualifies: The largely unfolded state B is seen as its own peak set (CEST on both A and B peaks, zz-exchange) and exchanges on a 300 ms scale in the perdeuterated sample. B is the unfolded domain, not the α-hairpin; the sub-millisecond states A', B' and B'' are dark and seen only through CPMG and CEST.
basis: The isolated wild-type CTD has two kinds of minor state. On the sub-millisecond scale, a joint 15N CPMG/CEST five-state fit over 35 residues finds the folded barrel exchanging with a dark state A' of about 0.35%, placed in the β1/β2 loop, while the unfolded state B exchanges with B' and B''. More slowly, the barrel unfolds and refolds: CEST gives a 5.5% unfolded-like state in protonated samples and about 25% in perdeuterated samples. None of these minor states is the NTD-bound α-hairpin.
kex: A'↔A τex about 500 µs (Results and Fig. 6; the abstract says about 1 ms) (RFAHTD-J4, RFAHTD-r9, RFAHTD-r13). B↔B' τex about 1.2–1.3 ms; B↔B'' about 800 µs (branched) or B'↔B'' about 1 ms (linear); linear-model kBB' 21.6 ± 2.4 s-1, kB'B 675 ± 25 s-1 (RFAHTD-J5, RFAHTD-r14). A↔B folding/unfolding: kex 14.80 ± 1.31 s-1 (kAB 0.82 ± 0.10, kBA 13.98 ± 1.24 s-1), protonated (RFAHTD-J7, RFAHTD-r5); kAB about 0.8 s-1, kBA about 2.4 s-1, τex about 300 ms, perdeuterated (RFAHTD-J6, RFAHTD-r8).
pB: A' about 0.35% (A about 76–77%); B' about 0.25–0.35%; B'' about 0.05% (RFAHTD-J4, RFAHTD-J5, RFAHTD-r9). Unfolded B: 5.53 ± 0.46% (reported with pA 94.47 ± 0.46%), protonated (RFAHTD-J7, RFAHTD-r5); about 25% (pA about 75%) by two-site CEST and about 23% in the five-state fit, perdeuterated (RFAHTD-J6, RFAHTD-r8, RFAHTD-r9).
regime: B is in slow exchange: separate A and B peaks with zz-exchange assignments, and CEST Δω(B−A) matches those assignments (RFAHTD-J6). A', B' and B'' are dark states seen only through dispersion and CEST; no Δω for them is printed in the rows (RFAHTD-J4, RFAHTD-J5).
residues: 35 residues in the five-state fit (SI Tables S3–S6): T109, Y111, a G113–F123 subset, G125, Q127, I129, D134–E136, R138–I146, K148, I150, V154, K155, E158–R160, L162 (T109 lies outside the entry); A' proposed as a β1/β2-loop change (RFAHTD-J4). 45 sites with A and B CEST profiles, T109–L162 (RFAHTD-J6). B' and B'' differ in helix α5* of the unfolded ensemble (RFAHTD-J5).

structure_match.what: Full-length RfaH crystal with the CTD as an α-hairpin packed on the NTD, the other fold of the same sequence (the isolated barrel is 2LCL). It does not match any isolated-CTD minor state: the minor ensemble resembles the urea-unfolded CTD with residual structure, not the α-hairpin, and free full-length RfaH does not visit the β state above 0.2%.

fallback_annotation: May have alternate states of the isolated CTD: a sub-millisecond β1/β2-loop state (about 0.35%) and a slowly exchanging, largely unfolded state (5.5% to about 25% depending on the sample), based on 15N CPMG and CEST (doi:10.1073/pnas.2506441122; doi:10.7554/elife.76630).
other_conditions: Full-length autoinhibited RfaH, 16 °C, pH 6.5, 50 mM sodium phosphate, 5% glycerol, 1 bar: yes. kAB 16.3 ± 1.2, kBA 319 ± 20 s-1 (τex about 3 ms), pB 4.9 ± 0.5%, mostly NTD β3/β4 with small Δω in the CTD helices (RFAHTD-J16, RFAHTD-r26).
Same sample at 2.5 kbar: yes. kAB 8.4 ± 0.4, kBA 202 ± 9 s-1, pB 4.0 ± 0.1% by CEST; CPMG curves are flat (RFAHTD-J17, RFAHTD-r27, RFAHTD-r28).
Full-length RfaH, 288 K, pH 7.5: no_evidence at CTD F123, G135, M140 and L145 by 15N CPMG, nuCPMG 30–2000 Hz (RFAHTD-J18, RFAHTD-r18).
Full-length RfaH, 298 K: no_evidence for the β-barrel CTD state above 0.2% at 20–200 s-1 by CEST (RFAHTD-J19, RFAHTD-r17).
ops-paused elongation complex bound: the tethered CTD converts from α to β and returns toward α on competitive release; titration endpoints, no rate (RFAHTD-J12, RFAHTD-r20, RFAHTD-r21).
Homolog V. cholerae RfaH-KOW, 25 °C: yes (homolog). pB 0.43 ± 0.01% (pA 99.57 ± 0.01%), kex 74.57 ± 3.18 s-1 (RFAHTD-J31, RFAHTD-r7).
caveats: The unfolded-state population differs between the protonated (5.5%) and perdeuterated (about 25%) samples, which also differ in buffer and construct start; kAB agrees but kBA does not, and the rows do not say which difference causes it. The A' lifetime is printed as about 500 µs and about 1 ms in the same paper. Linear and branched five-state schemes fit equally well. The judgments place the folding/unfolding exchange in the slower-than-ms window. The RelaxDB R1/R2/NOE sample is unidentified (the likely Tudor-domain paper was read as abstract only).

protein: Bacillus subtilis SigA (σA) domain 1.1, author residues 1–71 plus LE-His6
reference_state: Wild-type free domain 1.1 (no RNAP or DNA), 25 °C (methanol-calibrated); buffer and pH not stated in the paper (the deposition lists pH 6.6, 10 mM ionic strength)
literal_two_peak: does not (computed): the authors call it 'slow exchange' in the µs-ms sense, but kex ~3,500 (printed as Hz) against 15N Δω 2-6 ppm gives kex/Δω about 1.0-4.6 at 600-950 MHz, i.e. intermediate to fast, and no minor-state peaks are shown (computed by Claude 2026-10-20 after the night review; replaces 'qualifies by wording only').
basis: Model-free fits at three fields need exchange terms at many residues in helix I and the regions packed against it. 15N CPMG at 600, 850 and 950 MHz fits a two-state process with a fairly uniform rate and a representative 1.5% minor state whose 15N shifts differ by 2–6 ppm. The per-residue fits are figure-only, and the minor-state structure is unknown.
kex: ~3,500, printed as Hz (SIGA-J6, SIGA-r3)
pB: 1.5%, the authors' representative value from the two-state model (SIGA-J6, SIGA-r3)
regime: Called 'slow exchange' by the authors in the µs-ms sense (SIGA-r3 source, Discussion and Fig. 3 caption). 15N Δω 2–6 ppm, largest at the end of helix I, in helix II and in the β-sheet (SIGA-J6).
residues: Rex: helix I (F12–R26, especially its ends), the C-terminal part of helix II (Y31–F41), the β-sheet and its vicinity, figure-only (SIGA-J5, SIGA-r2). CPMG: largest Δω at the end of helix I, in helix II and in β-sheet II; E21 and D46 are named only for pB standard deviations of 0.087 and 0.089; residue set figure-only (SIGA-J6).
fallback_annotation: May have an alternate conformation differing at the end of helix I, in helix II and in the β-sheet, based on 15N CPMG relaxation dispersion and multi-field 15N relaxation of the free domain (doi:10.1074/jbc.m117.784074).
other_conditions: 2023 abstract, construct not stated, room temperature: possible. A transiently occupied, partially unfolded minor state with reduced helix I and helix III structure holds about 4% of molecules and rises with temperature; method, construct and rate not readable (SIGA-J7, SIGA-r1).
caveats: No structure is matched: 5MWW is the dominant free fold, and the authors' suggestion that the minor state resembles the T. maritima fold is speculative (SIGA-r3, SIGA-r6). The 4% state of the 2023 abstract cannot be assumed to be the 1.5% CPMG state. In the BMRB 27011 deposition the R2 error column exceeds the value in most rows, so the columns may be swapped; this deposition screen does not set the call. kex is kept as printed ('~3,500 Hz').

protein: Pseudomonas aeruginosa PSE-4 class A β-lactamase, wild-type mature enzyme (271 residues; the paper uses Ambler numbering)
reference_state: Free wild-type enzyme, no substrate or inhibitor, 31.5 °C, pH 6.65, no buffer (phosphate deliberately omitted), 3 mM imidazole, 0.1% sodium azide, 10% D2O, 0.5 mM 15N
literal_two_peak: cannot tell: No regime is stated and no dispersion was recorded; S70 and A237 are broadened out and K73's weak peak points to slow or intermediate exchange, but no second peak set is reported.
basis: The field dependence of 15N R2 at 50.6 and 60.8 MHz needs exchange terms at 32 amides, most prominently T128, L221, R234, S235 and G236 near the active site and R161 and R178 at the ends of the Ω loop. The catalytic S70 and A237 amides are broadened out. No CPMG or R1rho was recorded, so there is no rate or population.
kex: not measured (PSE4-J5, PSE4-J7). Rex where given, scaled to 60.8 MHz 15N: R234 4.2 ± 1.6 s-1, S235 7.5 s-1, G236 4.5 s-1 (PSE4-J5, PSE4-r2).
pB: not measured (PSE4-J5). The H/D-exchange estimate of a >0.1% partially unfolded population rests on an assumed free energy, not a fit (PSE4-J12).
regime: Not stated. K73 has no Rex in the best model, but its weak amide peak and missing side-chain signals point to slow or intermediate exchange that the quadratic Rex scaling may miss (PSE4-J9).
residues: T128, L221, R234, S235, G236 (entry 106, 199, 212, 213, 214) near the active site (PSE4-J5); R161 and R178 (entry 139, 156) at the Ω-loop ends (PSE4-J6); 32 Rex sites in all, figure-only (PSE4-J7); S70 and A237 not observed (PSE4-J8). No Rex inside the Ω loop or at S106 (PSE4-J10, PSE4-J11).
fallback_annotation: May have an alternate conformation near the active site and at the Ω-loop hinges (R161, R178), based on two-field 15N R2 exchange terms and amide H/D exchange of the free enzyme (doi:10.1016/j.bpj.2009.02.068).
other_conditions: Same sample, amide H/D exchange (slower than ms): I97–Q115 and N132–I137 exchange within the 32 min dead time, as do E171–L177 and S235/G236, while R161–N170 and most secondary structure are protected (about 6–11 kcal/mol). These are solvent-exchange rates, not opening rates or populations (PSE4-J12 to PSE4-J16, PSE4-r3, PSE4-r4).
Proposed cavity-filling motion of E171–L177 toward R65, hinged at R161/R178, rests on a TEM-1 homolog simulation; no PSE-4 alternate state was measured (PSE4-J17, PSE4-r2).
Wild-type crystal versus R234K: an alternate S130 side-chain conformation, abstract only, no rate (PSE4-J18, PSE4-r5).
caveats: Rex rests on two fields (the 81.0 MHz R2 was excluded) with quadratic field scaling. The BMRB 6838 deposition screen flags T128, L221, S235 and G236 and not R234, whose 500 MHz R2 is lowered by overlap with K192; the screen does not set the call. The full Rex and exchange tables (SI) were unavailable. No PDB entry is named for the S130 alternate, so no structure is matched.

protein: Human REV1 C-terminal domain (Rev1-CT, 1157–1251, G1157 remnant after TEV cleavage)
reference_state: Free wild-type Rev1-CT, no peptide, 15 °C, pH 7.0, 50 mM NaH2PO4, 100 mM NaCl, 0.25 mM EDTA, 5 mM DTT, 0.9 mM 15N/13C; 11.7 T
literal_two_peak: cannot tell: No regime is stated for the free domain and no apo Δω is printed; F1165 and S1223 are broadened beyond detection, and no second peak set is reported.
basis: 15N CPMG at 11.7 T shows millisecond exchange at the RIR-binding pocket, with dispersion at G1161, L1171, W1175 and D1186, and model-free Rex in the H1–H2 and H3–H4 loops. No apo rate or population was fitted. The only fitted rate and population come from the 89%-bound pol η RIR complex and may include peptide on–off exchange.
kex: not fitted for the free domain (REV1CT-J3, REV1CT-r2)
pB: not fitted for the free domain (REV1CT-J3); 5.9 ± 0.4% only in the pol η RIR complex (REV1CT-J7, REV1CT-r5)
regime: Not stated. Dispersion plateaus near 500 Hz at the example residues (REV1CT-J3); the 500 Hz CPMG R2 used for model-free Rex suppresses slow exchange, so that Rex reports the faster part of the exchange (buffer note).
residues: RIR-binding pocket: G1161, L1171, W1175, D1186 (entry 5, 15, 19, 30), author-listed examples; the figure-only exchange map (Fig. 5C) also marks the β-hairpin, the last two turns of H1, the H1–H2 loop and the first two turns of H2 (REV1CT-J3). F1165 and S1223 not detected (REV1CT-J4).
fallback_annotation: May have an alternate conformation at the pol η RIR-binding pocket (β-hairpin, helices H1 and H2), based on 15N CPMG relaxation dispersion and model-free Rex of the free domain (doi:10.1021/bi300566z).
other_conditions: Pol η RIR complex, about 89% bound, 15 °C: possible. Two-field global fit kex 585 ± 23 s-1, pB 5.9 ± 0.4%, which mixes peptide binding with possible intramolecular exchange (about twice the 300 s-1 on–off upper bound; Δω mostly matches free–bound differences) (REV1CT-J7, REV1CT-r5); model-free Rex at 1175–1179 (REV1CT-J6, REV1CT-r4); F1165, S1223 and V1224 missing (REV1CT-J8, REV1CT-r6).

protein: Chicken (Gallus gallus) villin-1 domain 6 (V6), isolated, 107 residues (2LLF chain A)
reference_state: Calcium-free wild-type isolated V6 (the 107-residue entry sequence); no evidence row measures it. The RelaxDB source paper measured D6-HP (208 residues) in 5 mM calcium at 25 °C, pH 7.0, a different construct and ligand state.
literal_two_peak: cannot tell: nothing measures the calcium-free isolated domain. In calcium-bound D6-HP the authors attribute the missing P68-D72 and E85 amides to intermediate exchange on the NMR timescale, which would not qualify, and no second peak set is reported (VILD6-J7).
basis: No evidence row measures dynamics of calcium-free isolated D6 in any window (VILD6-J2 to J4). The RelaxDB source paper (doi:10.1021/bi700110v, read in full) is on the larger D6-HP construct in 5 mM calcium: the D6 region 1-105 is structured on the ps-ns scale apart from F84 (VILD6-J5, J6); the P68-D72 loop and E85 are missing from the HSQC with intermediate exchange proposed and no rate or population (VILD6-J7); calcium removal makes a quarter of D6 amides disappear or shift in the first 80 residues, confounded by aggregation (VILD6-J8). Exchange seen only in another construct and bound state is not exchange in the reference state, so the call stays unknown.
kex: not measured (VILD6-J3); the D6-HP missing peaks carry no rate (VILD6-J7)
pB: not measured (VILD6-J3); 'one quarter of D6 amides' on calcium removal is a count of affected peaks, not a population (VILD6-J8)
regime: Not measured for the reference state (VILD6-J3). Calcium-bound D6-HP: 'intermediate structural exchange on the NMR time scale' proposed for P68-D72 and E85 (VILD6-J7).
residues: none measured in the reference state. Calcium-bound D6-HP: P68-D72 and E85 missing (intermediate exchange proposed), A60-E62 missing and unexplained, F84 mobile on the ps-ns scale (VILD6-J5, J7); calcium-free D6-HP: first 80 residues affected, no list (VILD6-J8)

structure_match.what: Calcium-bound NMR structure of isolated V6 with an extended long helix. A ligand-bound form, not an apo minor state; the gelsolin-like straightening pathway is proposed, not experimentally resolved.

fallback_annotation: No apo alternate-state annotation is possible for isolated V6. In the D6-HP construct with 5 mM calcium the D6 loop P68-D72 and E85 are broadened out, which the authors propose reflects intermediate exchange (doi:10.1021/bi700110v); isolated V6 changes conformation on calcium binding, centred on the long helix (doi:10.1021/bi400699s, abstract only).
other_conditions: D6-HP in 5 mM CaCl2, 25 °C, pH 7.0, 20 mM PIPES (RelaxDB source paper): D6 structured on the ps-ns scale except F84 (low R2, NOE below 0.6); P68-D72 and E85 missing from the HSQC, intermediate exchange proposed; no rate or population (VILD6-J5 to J7, VILD6-VILD6_20261020153804-r1, r2).

D6-HP without calcium: about one quarter of D6 amide peaks disappear or shift, in the first 80 residues; calcium-poor D6-HP aggregates within hours, so exchange, unfolding and oligomerisation cannot be separated (VILD6-J8, VILD6-VILD6_20261020153804-r3).

Calcium titration of isolated V6 (micromolar to millimolar): the long helix and its neighbours respond most to micromolar calcium, with tryptophan-fluorescence Kd values of 22 µM and 2.8 mM; an equilibrium, ligand-driven change with no rate, population or residue list (VILD6-J1, VILD6-r26).
caveats: The RelaxDB VILD6 relaxation set appears to come from D6-HP in 5 mM calcium (doi:10.1021/bi700110v, case S6_r6_VILD6_20261020153804, read in full on 2026-10-20), while the entry sequence is the isolated 107-residue D6; if the NMR collaborator sets the reference state to calcium-bound D6 within D6-HP, the call rises to possible on the missing P68-D72 and E85 amides. BMRB 18046 (cross-referenced by 2LLF) deposits no relaxation lists. Villin headpiece rows (VILD6-r1 to r25) are a separate domain and were not used.
