protein: Pseudomonas aeruginosa azurin (UniProt P00282), mature wild type A1-K128
reference_state: The RelaxDB sample: wild-type Pseudomonas aeruginosa azurin with its copper reduced to Cu(I) (dithionite), 2 mM, 20 mM potassium phosphate, pH 5.5, 41 °C, 600 MHz (doi:10.1021/bi990624l, full text; AZURIN-J37, J41-J43 marked is_wt_apo). Changed on 2026-10-20 from copper-free apo, which stays in the table as another sample state (AZURIN-J18 to J26). Reduced Cu(I) holo azurin is the deposited construct's native metal state; the alternate state here is still a metal-bound, protonation-coupled one.
literal_two_peak: qualifies: the source states that the His35 process is slow on the chemical-shift timescale at both pH 7.0 and pH 5.5 and shows two resolved peak sets for the protons and nitrogens around His35 in jump-return HMQC spectra between pH 6.3 and 7.6, connected by EXSY/ROESY cross-peaks at pH 7.0 (AZURIN-J38; D-r4, D-r5). Computed regime (E-033): kex = kAB + kBA = 2k = 90 ± 12 s-1 at pH 7.0 and 120 ± 60 s-1 at pH 5.5; 15N delta-omega 340 Hz (G37) to about 400 Hz (G88, G90) at 60.8 MHz, i.e. 2136-2513 rad/s; kex/delta-omega = 0.04 (pH 7.0) and 0.06 (pH 5.5), slow exchange, matching the authors' wording. At the reference pH 5.5 the minor form is only 2-4%, so the second peak set is documented near pH 7, not shown at pH 5.5.
basis: In the RelaxDB sample (reduced Cu(I), pH 5.5, 41 °C) the amides of N10, D11, G37, G45, G88, S89 and G90, all surrounding His35, carry exchange contributions of 2-9.5 Hz; the authors reproduce the broadening of G37, G88 and G90 with the His35 protonation/deprotonation equilibrium: deprotonated minor form 0.02-0.04 (from the pKa of 7.0 ± 0.1), k = 60 ± 30 s-1, lifetime 8 ± 4 ms, 15N shift differences 340-400 Hz (AZURIN-J43, D-r3). At pH 7.0 the two forms are equally populated, give two resolved peak sets and interconvert at k = 45 ± 6 s-1 (lifetime 11 ± 2 ms) by EXSY (AZURIN-J38, D-r4, D-r5). The authors identify the two forms with the pH 5.5 and pH 9.0 crystal conformations, which differ by a P36-G37 peptide flip and the loops 9-12 and 88-91 (AZURIN-J44, D-r6, oxidised crystals, structure_only). The 2003 three-field CPMG study of Cu(I) azurin at pH about 5 sees the same H35 region with a 0.39% minor state and kA 11.7 s-1 at 44.8 °C and a second copper-loop process (0.45%, kA 4.1 s-1) (AZURIN-J12, J13); its kinetic model disagrees with the 1999 rates. The call is 'yes' because the reference-state sample shows exchange that the same paper resolves as two peak sets with a measured rate; the caveat is that the alternate state is a protonation state coupled to a local backbone flip, not a ligand-free conformational excursion.
kex: Reference state, pH 5.5: k = 60 ± 30 s-1 printed as (kAB + kBA)/2, so kex = 120 ± 60 s-1, tau_ex 8 ± 4 ms (model estimate from line broadening of G37, G88, G90; AZURIN-J43, D-r3). pH 7.0 EXSY: k = 45 ± 6 s-1 (average rate at the pKa, kAB = kBA), kex = 90 ± 12 s-1, tau_ex 11 ± 2 ms (AZURIN-J38, D-r4). 2003 Cu(I) CPMG at 44.8 °C, pH about 5, 50 mM phosphate: forward rates kA 11.7 ± 2.4 s-1 (H35 region, keq 254 ± 31) and 4.1 ± 0.1 s-1 (copper loops, keq 222 ± 7), total kex not printed (AZURIN-J12, J13; keq values from Table 3 of that paper, not in a row). Not measured for Cu(II) or apo.
pB: Reference state, pH 5.5: deprotonated form 0.02-0.04, estimated from the His35 pKa 7.0 ± 0.1, not fitted (D-r3). pH 7.0: 0.5 (equal populations at the pKa, stated by the authors; D-r4). 2003 Cu(I) CPMG: 0.39 ± 0.07% (H35 region) and 0.45 ± 0.02% (copper loops) at 44.8 °C (J12, J13). Not measured for Cu(II) or apo.
regime: Authors (1999, Cu(I)): 'slow on the chemical shift time scale' at pH 7.0 and 5.5; two resolved peak sets near the pKa. Computed: kex/delta-omega = 90/2136 = 0.04 at pH 7.0 and 120/2136 = 0.06 at pH 5.5 (delta-omega 340 Hz for G37 at 60.8 MHz 15N; about 400 Hz for G88/G90 gives 0.04-0.05), slow exchange. 2003 Cu(I) CPMG: no regime statement; Carver-Richards fit with kA much smaller than kB (J12, J13). Apo: 'intermediate exchange' for the 17 missing amides (AZURIN-r44). Cu(II): not stated.
residues: Reference state Cu(I), pH 5.5: N10, D11, G37, G45, G88, S89, G90 around His35 (Rex 2-9.5 Hz) and F114 in the copper loop (mechanism unassigned); pH 7.0 EXSY: His35 C-epsilon1 H and the amides of G9, G37, G88, E91; the crystal comparison names G9-Q12, P36-G37, M44-G45, G88-E91 (J43, J38, J44). 2003 Cu(I) CPMG: D11, G37, G88-G90 (near H35) and N47, W48, F111-T113, G116, H117, L120, K122 (near copper) (J12, J13). Apo: A1-C3, G9-D11, N18, H35-L39, G45, H46, G88-E91 missing, dispersion at M44 and I87 (J18, J19).

structure_match.pdb: not given (oxidised Cu(II) crystals at pH 5.5 and pH 9.0, Nar et al.)
structure_match.what: The authors' model of the two exchanging forms: at low pH the P36 carbonyl accepts a hydrogen bond from protonated His35 N-delta1-H; at high pH the P36-G37 peptide bond flips and G37 HN hydrogen-bonds His35 N-delta1, with loops 9-12 and 88-91 adjusting. Oxidised crystals compared with reduced solution data; no solution structure of either form.

fallback_annotation: Reduced Cu(I) azurin at pH 5.5 and 41 °C has an alternate state around His35 populated at about 2-4%: the deprotonated His35 form with a flipped P36-G37 peptide plane and adjusted loops 9-12 and 88-91, exchanging with k = 60 ± 30 s-1 (lifetime 8 ± 4 ms) and resolved as two peak sets near pH 7 (EXSY k = 45 ± 6 s-1) (doi:10.1021/bi990624l). The 2003 three-field CPMG study of Cu(I) azurin adds a 0.45% copper-loop state (N47, W48, F111-T113, G116, H117, L120, K122) of unknown structure (doi:10.1110/ps.0225403).
other_conditions: WT, pH 7.0 (2 mM nonlabelled sample) and pH 6.3-7.6 titration (15N sample), 20 mM phosphate, 41 °C; redox state not restated for these samples, inferred Cu(I) from the sample preparation and the reduced-form pKa (RelaxDB source paper, full text): yes, literal two-peak. Two resolved peak sets around His35, pKa 7.0 ± 0.1, EXSY k = 45 ± 6 s-1, equal populations, lifetime 11 ± 2 ms (AZURIN-J38; D-r4, D-r5).

Reduced Cu(I) WT, pH about 5, 50 mM phosphate, 25.7-44.8 °C (2003 three-field CPMG): yes. Two processes with minor states of 0.39% and 0.45% at 44.8 °C and forward rates of 11.7 and 4.1 s-1; the H35 process tracks H35 protonation, the copper-loop process has no known structure; oxidised contamination is ruled out at ≤0.2% (AZURIN-J12 to AZURIN-J16). Its kinetic model does not agree with the 1999 rates (open conflict).

Copper-free apo WT, 298 K, pH 7.0, 100 mM phosphate, 2 mM DTT: possible. 17 amides around the metal site are broadened out by intermediate exchange and CPMG dispersion is seen at M44, I87 and nearby regions, with no rate or population (AZURIN-J18, AZURIN-J19); T61 is flat (AZURIN-J20). Abstract-only leads: two apo crystal forms that differ at H46 and H117 and pH-dependent histidine broadening (AZURIN-J21, AZURIN-J22). Until 2026-10-20 this was the reference state.

Oxidised Cu(II) WT: unknown; no exchange measurement in the evidence (AZURIN-J2, J3). A temperature-jump slow phase in the azurin/cytochrome c551 mixture is assigned to the H35 relaxation, no rate (AZURIN-J39, abstract).
Zn-, Cd-, Co- and Fe-substituted WT: unknown. Only MD, phosphorescence and static crystals exist (AZURIN-J28 to AZURIN-J32).

Ru- and Re-labelled constructs and the N42C dye-labelled smFRET construct: not assessable; their kinetics are electron transfer and photophysics, not conformational exchange (AZURIN-J33 to AZURIN-J35).
caveats: Call raised from possible to yes on 2026-10-20 after the RelaxDB source paper (doi:10.1021/bi990624l) was read in full and the reference state was reset to its sample, reduced Cu(I) azurin at pH 5.5 and 41 °C (ledger/redraft_notes.json; adjudication ledger/adjudication_AZURIN_pdf.json). Two caveats for the NMR collaborator: (1) the alternate state is protonation-coupled, a pH-dependent chemical equilibrium of His35 with a local peptide flip, and its 2-4% population at pH 5.5 is estimated from the pKa rather than fitted; (2) the reference state is metal-bound (Cu(I) holo), so this is not a ligand-free alternate conformation in the strict sense. The pH 5.5 rate comes from single-field line broadening with an equal-population equation corrected for unequal populations (k = 60 ± 30 s-1); the two-peak evidence and the EXSY rate come from pH 7.0 samples, where the populations are equal. The 2003 three-field CPMG model of the same Cu(I) H35 process (pB 0.39%, kA 11.7 s-1, kex in the thousands per second) is not reconciled with the 1999 rates. The abstract-only rows of the 1999 paper (AZURIN-AZURIN_20261020143153-r1, r2) are superseded and no longer cited. Only the selected papers were searched, all in phosphate or Tris.

protein: Bovine calbindin D9k (protein S100-G, UniProt P02633), 75 residues; the entry sequence is the P43G variant
reference_state: Ca2+-free (apo) calbindin D9k in the entry construct P43G (the entry sequence carries G43), as measured in the RelaxDB source paper (doi:10.1021/bi00088a039, full text): 4 mM uniformly 15N P43G, 300 K, pH 6.0 (HCl, no buffer), 95% H2O/5% D2O, 11.74 T, single field (CD9K-J12, J13 marked is_wt_apo). The paper states that all its studies use P43G.
literal_two_peak: cannot tell: for apo P43G the source states no exchange regime, prints no kex or Δω and shows no second peak set; exchange appears only as single-field model-free Rex at 14 amides, and the authors say further kinetic analysis is not possible (CD9K-J13, E-r4). P43G exists as a single isoform, so the two peak sets in slow exchange (3:1, 2D exchange) of native Pro43 calbindin in the Ca2+-loaded state (CD9K-J1; CD9K-r4, r9) do not exist in the entry construct.
basis: Reference state: in the RelaxDB source sample (apo P43G, 300 K, pH 6.0, 11.74 T) 14 backbone amides need an exchange term, largest at A15 (2.39 s-1) and D19 (1.32 s-1) in the unoccupied site I loop and at K55 and V61 (1.11 s-1) in loop II, with E17 0.89, I73 0.65 and the rest 0.32-0.56 s-1; the authors attribute it to intrinsic conformational heterogeneity, excluding exchange with the below-0.5% Ca2+-loaded contaminant (koff below 20 s-1), and give no rate, population or substate structure (CD9K-J13, E-r4). Under the single-field Rex rule of 2026-10-20 this is exchange detected in the reference state without a population, so the call is 'possible'. Context from the same paper: with one Cd2+ in site II the unoccupied loop I broadens much more strongly (A14, K16, G18, D19, Q22; E17 and S24 lost), read as more frequent sampling of loop-I substates (CD9K-J15, E-r5), and the Ca2+-loaded protein shows no significant exchange (42 terms at or below 0.33 s-1; CD9K-J37, E-r6). No dispersion, R1rho or CEST study of apo P43G exists in the evidence; the millisecond R1rho exchange is reported only for Ca2+-loaded P43M (CD9K-J27, abstract).
kex: not reported for apo P43G; Rex only, 0.32-2.39 s-1 at 14 residues (CD9K-J13, E-r4). The authors' 1 ms CPMG spacing argument (rates comparable to 2000 s-1) is an instrumental sensitivity statement, not a fitted rate.
pB: not reported for apo P43G (CD9K-J13); the only population-like numbers are contamination bounds (Ca2+-loaded below 0.5% in apo; Cd2-loaded fraction below 0.05 in (Cd2+)1).
regime: Not stated for apo P43G (CD9K-J13). No Δω printed. The authors state that the chemical shifts of the discrete substates cannot be determined, which is why no kinetic analysis follows.
residues: Apo P43G (Table I Rex, s-1): G8 0.48, A14 0.44, A15 2.39, K16 0.40, E17 0.89, D19 1.32, L30 0.33, E35 0.56, E51 0.56, D54 0.33, K55 1.11, V61 1.11, V68 0.32, I73 0.65; Q75 R2 excluded for exchange (CD9K-J13). (Cd2+)1 P43G: A14, K16, G18, D19, Q22 substantial; E17, S24 undetected; A15, L23 unfittable; 21 numeric entries in all (CD9K-J15).
fallback_annotation: May have alternate conformations of the unoccupied site I loop (A14-D19) and of loop II (D54-V61) in apo P43G calbindin D9k: single-field 15N model-free exchange terms of up to 2.39 s-1 (A15) at 300 K, pH 6.0, attributed by the authors to intrinsic conformational heterogeneity (doi:10.1021/bi00088a039); no rate, population or substate structure.
other_conditions: (Cd2+)1 P43G, 300 K, pH 6.0, 11.74 T (RelaxDB source paper, full text): possible. Strong single-field exchange broadening in the unoccupied site I loop (A14, K16, G18, D19, Q22; E17, S24 lost; A15, L23 unfittable), assigned to substates of the singly loaded protein rather than Cd2+ exchange (Cd2-loaded fraction below 0.05, koff 700 s-1, Rex uncorrelated with shift difference); no rate or population (CD9K-J15, E-r5).
(Ca2+)2 P43G, single-field reanalysis of the 1992 data: no second peak set and no significant exchange, 42 fitted Rex terms all at or below 0.33 s-1 (CD9K-J37, E-r6; CD9K-J6 abstract).

Native Pro43, Ca2+-loaded: yes for a literal two-peak state. Two folded forms, 3:1 trans:cis at the Gly42-Pro43 bond, interconvert slowly (cis-to-trans 0.2 s-1 at 25 °C, extrapolated from line shapes); abstracts only (CD9K-J1; CD9K-r4, CD9K-r9). This is proline isomerism in the linker, absent from the entry construct.
Native Pro43, apo: cannot tell. The apo P43G assignment abstract says the wild type was set aside for conformational heterogeneity, but no row shows apo peak sets or a rate (CD9K-J7, CD9K-r11).
P43M, dicalcium and Ca/La: possible lead only. Millisecond equilibria at S38, G42-S44, L46 and G18, D19 by R1rho, lost in 2 M GdmHCl (CD9K-J27 to CD9K-J29, abstracts).
P43M and Q22N/P43M under crystallization conditions: domain-swapped dimers form over about 30 days, an intermolecular kinetic trap, not a monomer state (CD9K-J31).
caveats: Call raised from unknown to possible on 2026-10-20 after the RelaxDB source paper (doi:10.1021/bi00088a039) was read in full: exchange is detected in the reference state (apo P43G, 300 K, pH 6.0) as single-field model-free Rex at 14 amides, and under the single-field Rex rule decided that night (ledger/redraft_notes.json, _RULE_single_field_rex) this counts as exchange detected without a population. Fixed caveat: single-field Rex can also come from anisotropic tumbling; a dispersion experiment would confirm. The construct question is settled (P43G for every sample in the paper), and P43G removes the Pro43 cis/trans two-isoform spectra, so no literal two-peak state exists in the entry construct. The apo sample has no buffer solute (pH set with HCl) and the Ca2+-loaded data are a reanalysis of a 1992 sample whose composition is not restated. Deamidation at N56 during urea preparation can create extra species that mimic a second conformer (CD9K-J26). The abstract-only rows CD9K-r2 and CD9K-r3 are superseded and no longer cited. the NMR collaborator is asked whether the RelaxDB set is the apo, (Cd2+)1 or Ca2+-loaded P43G sample.

protein: Human CCL5/RANTES variant 5P12-RANTES-E66S (the entry sequence; engineered N terminus Q0-S9 and E66S, author Q0-S68 = entry 1-69)
reference_state: Free monomeric 5P12-RANTES-E66S, no detergent or receptor; 37 °C, pH 3.8, 50 mM KH2PO4, 0.02% NaN3, 5% D2O, 0.6 mM (BMRB metadata says 273 K, unresolved)
literal_two_peak: cannot tell: For the entry construct the source reports one concentration-independent resonance set and states no exchange regime for the raised R2 at M5-S9 or the broadening at Y14 and G32; the separate monomer and dimer peak sets reported for native-N-terminus E66S CCL5 belong to self-association, not to an alternate monomer state.
basis: In free 5P12-RANTES-E66S the µs-ms signs are qualitative: raised 15N R2 at M5–S9 inside the frayed N-terminal tail, and exchange broadening at Y14 and G32 that the authors exclude from core averages. No dispersion was recorded, so there is no rate, population or Δω, and the construct stays monomeric. The call is possible on exchange broadening alone; the two-peak observations in CCL5 (monomer and dimer, 12AAA14 heterogeneity) are self-association or anion effects in other constructs and are kept out.
kex: not measured (R19335-J3, R19335-J4)
pB: not measured (R19335-J3, R19335-J4)
regime: Not stated for the entry construct (R19335-J3, R19335-J4). In Fos-Choline-12 micelles the authors name intermediate exchange as one possible cause of the dark core, a detergent-denatured state (R19335-J7).
residues: M5-S9 (entry 6-10, raised R2) and Y14, G32 (entry 15, 33, exchange broadening) (R19335-J3, R19335-J4).
fallback_annotation: No alternate-state annotation is supported: free 5P12-RANTES-E66S shows only qualitative µs-ms signs at M5-S9 and at Y14 and G32 from 15N R2, with no dispersion, rate or second peak set (doi:10.1016/j.bpj.2013.10.025).
other_conditions: Native-N-terminus E66S CCL5, pH 4.8 acetate, 310 K and 293 K: separate monomer and dimer peaks (IM/ID 0.45 to 0.13 on cooling); self-association, not an alternate monomer state (R19335-J10, R19335-r8, R19335-r9).
Native-N-terminus E66S CCL5, pH 4.5, 37 °C, 1 versus 20 µM: two signal sets at 20 µM from monomer and dimer; self-association (R19335-J11, R19335-r34).

CCL5-12AAA14 mutant, pH 3.2, 298 K: heterogeneous spectrum that sulfate collapses to one dimer set, and missing basic-residue peaks possibly from intermediate exchange with sulfate; unknown (R19335-J15, R19335-J16).
Fos-Choline-12 micelles, pH 3.8: core NMR-dark at 25 °C, back at 60 °C as a non-native helical ensemble; artefact suspected (R19335-J7).
Receptor peptide or Evasin-4 bound: fast or intermediate binding exchange; binding kinetics, not an apo state (R19335-J18 to R19335-J22).
caveats: The entry construct is itself an engineered variant; native CCL5 data are other constructs. The deposited core averages equal the paper's 37 °C values although the BMRB metadata says 273 K. All entry data are in phosphate without a control. The deposition readback (R2/R1 screen flags Y15) is a lead only.

protein: Mouse SPRY domain-containing SOCS box protein 2 (SPSB2/SSB-2, UniProt O88838), SPRY domain construct 12-224 (226 residues, 2AFJ:A)
reference_state: Free wild-type SSB-2 (12-224), no peptide or inhibitor; 22 °C, pH 7.0, 10 mM sodium phosphate, 50 mM NaCl, 2 mM EDTA, 0.02% NaN3; the input card gives no BMRB id
literal_two_peak: does not: The authors attribute the missing loop-CD amides H119-G125 to intermediate-timescale exchange; no second peak set is reported, and CPMG shows no dispersion in the observable amides.
basis: Seven loop-CD amides (H119-G125, entry 114-120) are absent at 5, 15 and 22 °C and at 500-800 MHz, and CLEANEX recovers none, so the authors attribute the loss to intermediate conformational exchange (SPRY-J4). 15N CPMG at 600 MHz, 22 °C finds no dispersion among observable amides (SPRY-J3), and apparent Modelfree Rex terms may be tensor bias (SPRY-J5). There is no rate, population, delta omega or minor-state structure.
kex: not measured (SPRY-J4); no dispersion at nuCPMG 20-1000 Hz in observable amides (SPRY-J3, SPRY-r2)
pB: not measured (SPRY-J4)
regime: Intermediate exchange, the authors' reading of absent cross-peaks after temperature, field and CLEANEX controls (SPRY-J4, SPRY-r3 to SPRY-r6); no dispersion was possible for these amides.
residues: loop CD H119-G125 (entry 114-120) (SPRY-J4); fast ps-ns motion separately in loop DE I135-E165 (SPRY-J1)
fallback_annotation: May have an alternate conformation of loop CD (H119-G125) relative to the beta-sandwich core, based on amide cross-peaks missing at all tested temperatures and fields that the authors attribute to intermediate exchange in the free SPRY domain (doi:10.1110/ps.062477806); no rate or population.
other_conditions: Murine SPSB2 bound to human Par-4(59-77), 295 K, pH 6.7: chemical-shift changes around the ELNNN site including loop D; a bound-state environment change, not an alternate state (SPRY-J10, SPRY-r15).

Human SPSB2 with VASA, iNOS, RGD and TAT peptides: crystal and SPR data only; modest rearrangements except W207, ligand binding kinetics and biphasic TAT dissociation, none a protein conformational exchange (SPRY-J11 to SPRY-J14).
Docked human SPSB2-CIGB-814 complex, one 100 ns MD run: fluctuating contacts, no alternate state (SPRY-J15).
caveats: The call rests on missing peaks, not dispersion; the NMR collaborator is asked whether that counts as µs-ms detection. Peptide- and inhibitor-bound states are kept out of the apo call. All mouse NMR is in phosphate/EDTA with no buffer control. No PDB entry is shown in the rows as a loop-CD alternate conformer, so no structure is matched.

protein: Human C->U-editing enzyme APOBEC-2 (UniProt Q9Y235), truncated A2 (41-224) with an SEF prefix (entry 4-187 = author 41-224), zinc bound
reference_state: Free truncated A2 (41-224), zinc bound, no substrate; 25 °C, pH 7.0, 20 mM HEPES, 50 mM NaCl, 5 mM DTT (paper's relaxation conditions; BMRB 18306 metadata says 310 K)
literal_two_peak: cannot tell: No row states an exchange regime for the entry construct; the paper reports a single resonance set (no tetramer doubling) and amides missing at 37 °C without a mechanism.
basis: No dispersion, R1rho or CEST exists for APOBEC2 (R18306-J2, search_insufficient). The 700 MHz relaxation data are readable only as an overall tumbling time of 17 ns (R18306-J1), and the amides missing from the truncated construct at 37 °C may reflect solvent exchange, precipitation or exchange (R18306-J3). Loop variability appears only in models and crystals (R18306-J5, R18306-J6).
kex: not measured (R18306-J2)
pB: not measured (R18306-J2)
regime: Not stated (R18306-J3).
residues: none localized; missing amides lie mostly in helices near the strand beta2 face, figure-only (R18306-J3)

structure_match.what: Truncated human A2 crystal tetramer in which the alpha1-beta1 loop is a loop in tetramer-interface subunits and a short strand in dimer-interface subunits; the authors attribute the difference to packing. Crystal snapshots, no solution population or rate, and the loop is disordered in their solution model.

fallback_annotation: No alternate-state annotation is possible for free truncated APOBEC2: no exchange measurement exists, and the alpha1-beta1 loop variability comes only from a restrained model and crystal subunits (doi:10.1021/bi300021s).
other_conditions: Full-length A2 (1-224), 37 °C: the N-terminal tail M1-E40, absent from the entry, is highly mobile by linewidths and shifts (R18306-J4).
Self-association: the entry construct is a monomer by SEC-MALS, tumbling and RDCs at 25 °C, unlike the crystal tetramer (R18306-J7).
Mouse A2 2RPZ homolog: different loop placement, not a measured transition (R18306-J6).
caveats: The deposited set flags Y89, C131 and I178 (entry Y52, C94, I141) by R2/R1, a lead that does not set the call. Figure S1 with the per-residue relaxation profile was not retrieved. Relaxation temperature conflicts between the paper (25 °C) and the deposition (310 K).

protein: Rat thyroid transcription factor 1 (Nkx2-1) homeodomain (UniProt P23441), 68 residues (1FTT:A; entry = author + 1)
reference_state: Free rat TTF-1 homeodomain as deposited (68 residues, segment 160-226 plus Met0), no DNA. The RelaxDB source sample (doi:10.1111/j.1742-4658.2007.06208.x, now full text): about 0.8 mM uniformly 15N-labelled protein, 286 +/- 0.5 K, pH 4.3 (uncorrected, set with HCl, no buffer salt), 95:5 H2O/D2O, 11.7 T, single field (R15521-J1, J2, J3, J9 marked is_wt_apo). The paper names BMRB 15521 as its deposition (p. 445), and the deposition metadata (500 MHz, 286 K, pH 4.3) match this sample.
literal_two_peak: cannot tell: the source states no exchange regime, prints no kex, population or Delta-omega and shows no second peak set; its phrase 'slow conformational exchange' means motion slower than the overall tumbling of 10.5 ns, inferred from one fitted Rex at Tyr25 and from excess J(0), not from an NMR slow-exchange regime (R15521-J1, J2; E-r2). Without kex and Delta-omega the E-033 computation cannot be made.
basis: Reference state: in the RelaxDB source sample (free homeodomain, 286 K, pH 4.3, 11.7 T) Tyr25 (entry 26) carries R2 26.39 s-1 where every other residue lies between 8.41 and 16.53 s-1, and its J(0) stands far above the rest; it is the only residue to which both the model-free and the spectral-density analysis assign an exchange contribution (R15521-J1, E-r2). The spectral-density analysis alone adds Lys21, Gln22, Ile38 and His52 (entry 22, 23, 39, 53) at the ends of helices I, II and III, which the authors read as fraying transitions and ascribe to the model-free miss being caused by an overestimated tau_m (R15521-J2). Under the single-field Rex rule of 2026-10-20 this is exchange detected in the reference state without a population, so the call is 'possible'. Context from the same paper: tau_m 10.51 ns (MF) or about 9.85 ns (RSDM); Arg1-Leu7, Arg58-Gln59 and Ala60-Gln67 move far faster than the core, Arg53 is intermediate and looks like a hinge, and the helices Gln10-Gln22, Ala28-Ile38 and Thr43-Gln50 stay ordered (R15521-J3); the paper's own 10 ns MD reproduces this and is too short for the slower process (R15521-J9). The 1H NMR structure and hydrogen-exchange abstracts put a kink or tightening at Asn51-Arg53 in the same helix (R15521-J4, J5).
kex: not reported: the paper gives only R2 and spectral densities, with no fitted exchange rate; the quantity printed next to Tyr25 on p. 438 is '14.67 +/- 2.35 ns', a unit that cannot be an exchange rate and is not used here (R15521-J1)
pB: not reported (R15521-J1, J2)
regime: Not stated. No Delta-omega is printed and no kex is fitted, so no regime can be computed; the authors speak qualitatively of microsecond-to-millisecond motion and propose aromatic side-chain motion at Tyr25 and helix-end fraying for the other four residues (R15521-J1, J2).
residues: Tyr25 (entry 26) by both analyses, R2 26.39 s-1 against 8.41-16.53 s-1 elsewhere; Lys21, Gln22, Ile38, His52 (entry 22, 23, 39, 53) by spectral density mapping only (R15521-J1, J2). ps-ns mobility: Arg1-Leu7, Arg58, Gln59, Ala60-Gln67 (entry 2-8, 59, 60, 61-68), with Arg53 (entry 54) intermediate (R15521-J3).
fallback_annotation: May have slow motion at Tyr25 in the loop between helices I and II and at the helix ends Lys21, Gln22, Ile38 and His52: single-field 15N relaxation of the free homeodomain at 286 K, pH 4.3, gives Tyr25 an R2 of 26.39 s-1 against 8.41-16.53 s-1 elsewhere, with the authors proposing aromatic side-chain motion and helix-end fraying (doi:10.1111/j.1742-4658.2007.06208.x); no rate, population or second peak set, and the same helix carries a kink or tightening at Asn51-Arg53 by structure and hydrogen exchange (doi:10.1006/jmbi.1994.1012 and doi:10.1002/bip.360370106, abstracts).
other_conditions: Free homeodomain, 286 K, pH 4.3 (HCl, no buffer), 0.8 mM, 11.7 T single field (2008 RelaxDB source, full text): possible. Tyr25 exchange by both analyses, four helix-end residues by RSDM only; mobile tails and C-terminal helix III, tau_m 10.5 ns; 10 ns MD agrees (R15521-J1, J2, J3, J9; E-r1, E-r2, E-r3).
Free homeodomain, 1H NMR structure and amide H/D exchange (abstracts, conditions not given): helix III extension 51-59 structured but less rigid, with a discontinuity at Asn51-Arg53 (R15521-J4, J5).
Free homeodomain at neutral pH, limited proteolysis: the C-terminal region resists proteases, unlike the acidic-pH NMR picture; a condition and method difference (R15521-J6).
DNA-bound rat homeodomain: the C-terminal region becomes more protease-accessible, read as displacement from the core; abstract only (R15521-J7).
DNA-bound human NKX2-1 crystal: same fold and recognition mode as related complexes, no measured exchange (R15521-J8).
caveats: Call raised from unknown to possible on 2026-10-20 after the RelaxDB source paper (doi:10.1111/j.1742-4658.2007.06208.x) was read in full: exchange is detected in the reference state as a single-field model-free Rex at Tyr25 plus four RSDM-only sites, and under the single-field Rex rule decided that night (ledger/redraft_notes.json, _RULE_single_field_rex) author-reported Rex in the reference state counts as exchange detected without a population. Fixed caveat: single-field Rex can also come from anisotropic tumbling; a dispersion experiment would confirm. Four of the five sites rest on the spectral-density analysis alone, which is a different interpretation of the same three measurements, not independent replication, and the authors themselves propose aromatic side-chain motion rather than backbone exchange at Tyr25. The sample has no buffer salt and sits at pH 4.3 and 286 K, conditions far from the physiological state and from the proteolysis and calorimetry rows; the domain unfolds at 32 °C without salt. Glu17, Leu34 and Lys46 were excluded for overlap, and the authors question their own local correlation times. The abstract-only row R15521-r1 is superseded and no longer cited; everything else on the rat domain is still an abstract. Built from cases S6_r6_15521 (earlier screen) and S6_r6_15521_20261020220843, with the PDF adjudication in ledger/adjudication_pdf_batch2.json.

protein: Mouse collagen alpha-1(VII) vWFA2 subdomain (UniProt Q63870 1048-1238 with GRAMG prefix; entry = author - 1042)
reference_state: Free vWFA2 as deposited (the entry sequence with its GRAM prefix), no partner; the relaxation and RDC sample is 298 K, pH 7.4, 10 mM sodium phosphate, 10% D2O, 500 MHz, and the paper names BMRB 50020 as its deposition (R50020-J1). The second source (doi:10.1016/j.febslet.2011.04.071, now full text) uses the same buffer and temperature but a pTWIN1 intein construct whose residual tag is not stated, so its rows are kept as another construct (R50020-J6 to J9).
literal_two_peak: cannot tell: neither source states an exchange regime for the free domain or shows two peak sets. The only regime word in either paper, fast exchange on the chemical-shift timescale, describes binding to mFNIII-9 (KD 0.8 +/- 0.3 mM by SPR), which is a binding process (R50020-J8).
basis: No measurement of conformational exchange exists for free vWFA2. The relaxation study reports ps-ns loop flexibility at N1133, N1219, around A1205 and T1208 (R50020-J1) and the RDC outliers mark local solution-crystal differences without a timescale (R50020-J2, J3); no dispersion, R1rho, CEST or exchange-broadening experiment was done (R50020-J4). The 2011 paper, read in full on 2026-10-20, adds no relaxation data: its flexibility statements are a disagreement between scalar couplings and the TALOS+ prediction over residues 78-87 (entry 83-92), which the authors say 'may be in a flexible loop' (R50020-J6), 16 amides still protected after three days in D2O (R50020-J7), unassigned affinity-tag residues (R50020-J9), and fast-exchange binding to mFNIII-9 (R50020-J8). The single-field Rex rule does not apply, because no Rex is reported in either paper.
kex: not measured in either source (R50020-J4); the only kinetic statement is the qualitative fast exchange of mFNIII-9 binding (R50020-J8)
pB: not measured (R50020-J4)
regime: Not stated for any internal process; fast exchange is stated only for mFNIII-9 binding (R50020-J8). No kex and no Delta-omega are printed, so no regime can be computed.
residues: none for us-ms. ps-ns loops at N1133, N1219, around A1205 and T1208 (entry 91, 177, 163, 166) (R50020-J1); possible flexible loop at author 78-87 = entry 83-92 (R50020-J6); amides protected after three days: entry 13-18, 38, 39, 119-124, 147, 172 (author D8, V9, V10, F11, L12, L13, L33, V34, V114-V119, M142, F167) (R50020-J7)
fallback_annotation: No alternate-state annotation is possible for free vWFA2: relaxation shows only fast loop motion, RDCs only local solution-crystal differences (doi:10.1002/2211-5463.12807), and the second source gives a possible flexible loop at entry 83-92 and a protected sheet core from a two-point hydrogen-exchange experiment without any rate (doi:10.1016/j.febslet.2011.04.071).
other_conditions: Free vWFA2, 298 K, pH 7.4, 10 mM phosphate, 500 MHz (2019 source): unknown. ps-ns loop flexibility only; no exchange experiment (R50020-J1, J4).

Free mvWFA2 on the intein construct, 298 K, pH 7.4, 10 mM phosphate, 500 MHz (2011 source, full text): unknown. Residues 78-87 may be a flexible loop from a coupling/TALOS+ disagreement; no relaxation measurement (R50020-J6, J9).
Same construct in 100% D2O: 16 amides of the hydrophobic sheet core still present after three days; protection from two time points, no rate (R50020-J7).
With mFNIII-9 at about 1:2: fast exchange on the chemical-shift timescale, KD 0.8 +/- 0.3 mM; binding, not a conformational state (R50020-J8).
In PEG-hexanol or CTAB:PEG-hexanol alignment media: RDC outliers against the 6S4C crystal, outlier set changing with the medium; no timescale (R50020-J2, J3).
caveats: Call stays unknown after the second RelaxDB-linked source (doi:10.1016/j.febslet.2011.04.071) was read in full on 2026-10-20: that paper measures no relaxation and reports no exchange contribution, so the single-field Rex rule has nothing to act on, and its flexibility statements are a secondary-structure disagreement and a two-point hydrogen-exchange protection map. Its construct carries an unstated residual intein tag and the entry's GRAM prefix is not part of its numbered sequence, so those rows are kept as another construct; the entry = author + 5 mapping was fixed from the sequence printed on the Fig. 3a/3b axis (ledger/adjudication_pdf_batch2.json). The hydrogen-exchange sample is in 100% D2O at nominal pH 7.4 without a pD correction. The deposition flags seven residues by R2/R1 (author G1085, H1143, V1158, I1178, L1186, G1195, G1222) that neither paper discusses; a lead only. The poorly defined alpha5-beta6 loop in 6S4C is static crystal evidence, not a second state.

protein: Escherichia coli ribonuclease HI (UniProt P0A7Y4), wild-type 155-residue sequence with C13, C63, C133 (1RCH:A); no BMRB id on the input card
reference_state: Free wild-type E. coli RNase HI (entry sequence, Cys-containing), no Mg2+ or nucleic acid. The RelaxDB source sample (doi:10.1021/bi00020a003, full text): about 1 mM 15N protein, 27 °C, pH 5.5, 100 mM deuterated sodium acetate, 600 MHz, single field (RNASEHI-J38, J51, J52). The other us-ms evidence is at 14.1 T, 283-310 K, pH 5.5 (2019 methyl study, cysteine-free) and from a multifield backbone reanalysis without restated conditions (2026, cysteine-free data set).
literal_two_peak: cannot tell: the reference-state source (1995, full text) detects exchange only as a single-field model-free Δex term and states no exchange regime, prints no kex or Δω and shows no second peak set (RNASEHI-J52); the authors speak of 'exchange in the millisecond time scale' as the generic window of the Δex term. The 2019 methyl analysis of the cysteine-free handle exchange assumes the fast limit and the 2026 Rex comes from a B0-squared fit (RNASEHI-J47, J18), which would give 'does not' if those constructs counted; the only exchange-broadening regime statement concerns W85 of the Thermus homolog (RNASEHI-J14).
basis: Reference state: in the RelaxDB source sample (free WT, 27 °C, pH 5.5, acetate, 600 MHz) 21 backbone amides need a model-free exchange term, concentrated in helices I (M50, A51, A52, A55, L56, L59) and IV (V101, D102, D103, W104, L107, A109, A110, L111) with I78, I82, W90 (2.61 Hz, largest), K91, N100, W118 and E135; mean Δex 0.71 Hz; the authors read it as millisecond exchange and a possibly cooperative motion of the two adjacent helices, with no rate, population or minor-state structure (RNASEHI-J52, E-r2). Under the single-field Rex rule of 2026-10-20 this is exchange detected in the reference state without a population, so the call is 'possible'. Supporting, other construct: the handle-region exchange in cysteine-free RNase HI* (V98, V101, L103 methyls broadened at 283-310 K; backbone Rex above 1 s-1 at 40 amides with G77 4.00 ± 0.38 s-1 at 900 MHz; RNASEHI-J47, J18) and the 1998 helix-I exchange abstract (J42). Solution RDCs and the V101 rotamer population fit open/closed averaging of the handle, and MD samples both handle states (RNASEHI-J11, J10).
kex: not measured in the reference state: the 1995 paper gives Δex (Hz, line-width contribution) only, mean 0.71 Hz over 20 residues and 2.61 Hz at W90 (RNASEHI-J52). Other constructs: the 2019 study gives apparent activation energies of 45.4 ± 1.6 kJ/mol (V98), 23.7 ± 1.9 kJ/mol (V101) and 21.4 ± 3.0 kJ/mol (L103) from the temperature dependence of Delta-Rex under a fast-limit assumption, not kex (RNASEHI-J47); the 2026 reanalysis gives Rex, with G77 at 4.00 ± 0.38 s-1 at 900 MHz (RNASEHI-J18).
pB: not measured in the reference state (RNASEHI-J52); the fast-limit treatment of the cysteine-free handle exchange assumes a dominant state (RNASEHI-J47); V101 trans chi1 rotamer about 10% in WT and above 30% in V98A is a rotamer population, not the closed-handle population (RNASEHI-J11, RNASEHI-J12)
regime: Not stated for the reference state: single-field Δex with no Δω (RNASEHI-J52). Fast limit assumed by the 2019 analysis of cysteine-free protein (p1 much greater than p2) and implied by the B0-squared Rex fit of 2026; not independently determined. In the T. thermophilus homolog the W85 RDC could not be measured because of exchange broadening (RNASEHI-J14, homolog).
residues: Reference state (1995, single-field Δex): M50, A51, A52, A55, L56, L59, I78, I82, W90, K91, N100, V101, D102, D103 (entry L103), W104, L107, A109, A110, L111, W118, E135 (RNASEHI-J52). Cysteine-free handle region: V98, V101, L103 methyls at all three temperatures, I78 and I82 at 283 K (RNASEHI-J47); G77 and 39 further amides with Rex above 1 s-1, figure only (RNASEHI-J18); helix I, no list (RNASEHI-J42, abstract); RDC probes W85, T92, V101 (RNASEHI-J11); simulated glycine-rich G15/N16 minor state (J9, MD only)
fallback_annotation: May have an alternate conformation involving helices I (N44-A58) and IV (V101-A110), which carry single-field exchange terms in the free wild-type enzyme at 27 °C, pH 5.5 (mean Δex 0.71 Hz, W90 2.61 Hz; doi:10.1021/bi00020a003), and of the substrate-binding handle region (residues 81-101, closed versus open) measured in cysteine-free RNase HI*: methyl exchange broadening at V98, V101 and L103 across 283-310 K (doi:10.1007/s10858-019-00240-w), backbone Rex at G77 and 39 further amides (doi:10.1021/jacs.6c05843), and solution RDCs and valine rotamer populations interpreted with MD (doi:10.1021/acs.biochem.0c00500); no rate or population measured.
other_conditions: Free WT (entry sequence), 27 °C, pH 5.5, 100 mM acetate, 600 MHz single field (1995 RelaxDB source, full text): possible. Model-free Δex at 21 amides in helices I and IV, W90 largest; fast motion at the termini and five loops, rigid secondary structure (RNASEHI-J52, J38, J51; E-r1, E-r2).

Free cysteine-free RNase HI* (construct not stated in the 2019 paper; same pAED4 line), 14.1 T, pH 5.5, 283/300/310 K (2019 methyl Hahn echo): handle methyls V98, V101, L103 exchange-broadened at all temperatures, I78/I82 at 283 K; apparent activation energies only; fast-limit assumed (RNASEHI-J47, RNASEHI-RNASEHI_20261020150655-r13 to r16).

Free cysteine-free RNase HI* (stated for the 2025 data set), 500/700/900 MHz backbone reanalysis, conditions not restated (2026): Rex above 1 s-1 at 40 amides, G77 4.00 ± 0.38 s-1 (RNASEHI-J18, RNASEHI-RNASEHI_20261020150655-r19).
Free WT, 1998 abstract: exchange contribution in helix I, reduced in the quintuple mutant; the mutant gains exchange at the protrusion junction (RNASEHI-J42, J43).

Mg2+-bound WT, pD 6.2: possible. Active-site side chains broaden by 13C R1rho in two groups (N44, E57, D102 and D10, E48, D70, D134), but the broadening tracks the apo-to-Mg shift difference and cannot be separated from Mg2+ binding exchange (RNASEHI-J20).
Cysteine-free RNase HI*, about 298 K, pH 5.5 acetate: possible. Model-free Rex at the example residues V54 and G77, no dispersion or rate (RNASEHI-J19).
V98A mutant: handle shifted toward closed conformations (V101 trans rotamer above 30%), no rate (RNASEHI-J12, J13).
Mg2+ and Zn2+ crystal forms: metal positions and H124 coordination differ between crystal forms (7VSA, 7VSC, 7VSD; 7VSB, 7VSE), static and without timescale (RNASEHI-J26, J27).

Refolding from urea, cysteine-free protein: folding intermediates with phases of 120 mus and 3.1 ms, a 0.78 s-1 Icore-to-native step, and pulsed-labeling HX-MS protection of helix A before helix D; not native-state alternate states (RNASEHI-J21 to J23, J50).
caveats: Call set to possible on 2026-10-20 after the RelaxDB source paper (doi:10.1021/bi00020a003) was read in full: exchange is detected in the reference state (free WT, 27 °C, pH 5.5) as a single-field model-free Δex term at 21 amides, and under the single-field Rex rule decided that night (ledger/redraft_notes.json, _RULE_single_field_rex) author-reported Rex in the reference state counts as exchange detected without a population. Fixed caveat: single-field Rex can also come from anisotropic tumbling; a dispersion experiment would confirm. The 1995 analysis gives no kex, population, Δω or second peak set, so whether the exchanging state is slow enough for separate peaks is untested. The handle-region evidence with temperature dependence (2019, 2026) is from cysteine-free RNase HI* (the 2026 reanalysis uses the 2025 relaxometry data set, which its paper states is cysteine-free; the 2019 sample's construct is not stated) and stays other-construct support. The earlier 15N handle-exchange studies cited as refs 54-56 of the 2019 paper are still not in the evidence. protein: Human E2 ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme G1 (UBE2G1, UniProt P62253), full length 1-170
reference_state: Free full-length wild-type UBE2G1 as deposited (the entry sequence), no ubiquitin, UbV or E3. The 2015 NMR study (doi:10.1186/s40543-015-0068-z, now full text) measures exactly this: 0.8 mM perdeuterated 2H/13C/15N protein, M1-E170 after GST cleavage (two cloning residues G-2 and S-1 remain), 30 °C, pH 7.0, 50 mM HEPES, 100 mM NaCl, 5 mM DTT, 5% D2O, 800 MHz for relaxation and 900 MHz at 25 °C for the assignments (UBE2G1-J3, J4, J6 marked is_wt_apo).
literal_two_peak: cannot tell: the one study of free UBE2G1 fits no exchange term, states no regime and shows no second peak set; the only 'two-state exchange' in the evidence is ubiquitin attached to the Ube2r1 paralog (UBE2G1-r2, abstract only).
basis: The relaxation set behind this entry is now identified and read: the 2015 study measures R1, R2 and NOE at 800 MHz and 30 °C and reads the acidic loop 97-109 and the termini as more flexible than the core, which tumbles with a correlation time of roughly 12-14 ns (UBE2G1-J3). It fits no order parameters, internal correlation times, exchange rates or populations, and no dispersion, CEST or R1rho experiment of UBE2G1 exists (UBE2G1-J4), so the single-field Rex rule has nothing to act on and the call stays unknown. The gaps in its assignment table are proline and glycine chemistry, not exchange (UBE2G1-J6). The only structural comparison is static and shows almost no backbone change on UbV.G1.1 binding (UBE2G1-J2), and the only other NMR row is an abstract about the acidic loop binding donor ubiquitin in a conjugate (UBE2G1-J1).
kex: not measured (UBE2G1-J4): the 2015 study reports no exchange term
pB: not measured (UBE2G1-J4)
regime: Not measured (UBE2G1-J4). No kex and no Delta-omega are printed, so no regime can be computed.
residues: none for us-ms. ps-ns flexibility in the acidic loop 97-109 (P97 and P107 have no amide, so the range is a regional annotation) and at the termini (UBE2G1-J3); Y102-G103-Y104 is named only as a donor-ubiquitin contact (UBE2G1-J1). Figure 3 of the 2015 paper shows uncommented R2 values of about 37 s-1 near residue 27 and about 42 s-1 near residue 126, with 128-131 elevated, against a 20-25 s-1 baseline; a lead for a dispersion measurement, not an exchange claim.

structure_match.what: Apo UBE2G1 crystal (residues 8-160 plus tag), the reference for the UbV.G1.1-bound 6D68 superposition (RMSD 0.66 Å, 'virtually no differences'). A static ground-state structure, not a minor state.

fallback_annotation: No apo alternate-state annotation is possible for UBE2G1: its relaxation data show only faster local motion in the acidic loop 97-109 and at the termini, with no exchange analysis (doi:10.1186/s40543-015-0068-z), and backside binding of an engineered ubiquitin variant leaves its crystal backbone almost unchanged (doi:10.1016/j.jmb.2019.09.024).
other_conditions: Free full-length UBE2G1, 30 °C, pH 7.0, 50 mM HEPES, 100 mM NaCl, 5 mM DTT, 0.8 mM, 800 MHz (2015 study, full text): unknown. Acidic loop 97-109 and termini more flexible, tau_c roughly 12-14 ns, no exchange term fitted (UBE2G1-J3, J4).
Same protein at 25 °C and 900 MHz (TROSY assignments): the table gaps are proline and glycine chemistry, not exchange (UBE2G1-J6).
UbV.G1.1-bound full-length UBE2G1 (6D68, 2:2 strand-exchanged complex), crystal at 20 °C, pH 8.0: backbone RMSD 0.66 A to apo 2AWF; static, no rate (UBE2G1-J2, UBE2G1-r4).
Ubiquitin K48R oxyester conjugates of wild-type and Y102G/Y104G Ube2g1: NMR implicates the acidic loop in donor-ubiquitin binding; abstract only, no exchange parameters (UBE2G1-J1, UBE2G1-r1).

E1 charging and discharge assays of wild type and S26R with UbV.G1.1 (30 °C, pH 7.5, HEPES, Mg/ATP; discharge with EDTA and apyrase): product kinetics, not conformational exchange; not judged (UBE2G1-r5 to UBE2G1-r8).
caveats: Call stays unknown after the 2015 NMR paper (doi:10.1186/s40543-015-0068-z) was read in full on 2026-10-20. That paper supplies what the RelaxDB card was missing, an R1/R2/NOE set on free full-length UBE2G1 at 800 MHz and 30 °C, but it fits no exchange term and runs no dispersion experiment, so there is no author-reported Rex for the single-field Rex rule to act on and the us-ms window stays a search gap rather than a negative result. Its protein is the entry sequence plus two cloning residues (G-2, S-1) left by GST cleavage, and it is treated here as the entry construct. All relaxation values are read from Figure 3, a plot; the uncommented R2 outliers near residues 27 and 126 are recorded as a lead and are not counted as exchange. The protein runs at an apparent 25 kDa against a 20 kDa sequence mass, with no quantitative test for oligomerisation. The RelaxDB card still carries no BMRB id, so the identification is by matching conditions and content, not by accession. Ube2r1 rows (UBE2G1-r2, UBE2G1-r3) describe a paralog and were not used; the 2015 JBC paper remains an abstract.

protein: Human eukaryotic release factor 1 (eRF1, UniProt P62495) N-terminal domain, native 1-142 plus LE (entry 1-144); NMR sample carries a C-terminal His6. The card's UniProt P03355 is the Moloney murine leukemia virus Gag-Pol polyprotein and does not match the sequence or the evidence.
reference_state: Free isolated N-domain as deposited (entry sequence, His6-tagged in the sample), no mRNA, ribosome or other eRF1 domains; 298 K, pH 6.8, 10 mM sodium phosphate, 25 mM NaCl, about 2 mM beta-mercaptoethanol, about 1 mM protein (BMRB 18092 is this paper's deposition).
literal_two_peak: qualifies: The source shows duplicate peak sets for several residues in the free domain, intensity ratio about 5:1 (Supporting Fig. S1, Fig. 2B), which it reads as two conformational states; it states no exchange regime or rate.
basis: In one sample of the free domain, several residues give a second resolved peak set at 10-20% (major 80-90%), so a minor conformer exists that exchanges slowly on the chemical-shift timescale, if it exchanges at all; the authors place the largest shift differences at the interface of the beta-sheet core with helices alpha2 and alpha3 and propose a reorientation of those helices (R18092-J4). Single-field model-free Rex at I45, D54-G57, K63, N67 and E134-A135 points to millisecond motion in the same region, but the source does not show it is the same process (R18092-J3).
kex: not measured (R18092-J4); Rex without dispersion at I45, D54-G57, K63, N67, E134-A135 at 600 MHz, values only in an unread supplement (R18092-J3)
pB: 10-20% minor (major 80-90%; intensity ratio about 5:1), spectral estimates, not fitted populations (R18092-J4, R18092-r2)
regime: Not stated in words. Resolved peaks for both conformers mean exchange, if present, is slow relative to their shift differences; no Δω, exchange cross-peak or rate is reported (R18092-J4).
residues: doubled residues figure-only (Fig. 2B, Fig. S1), largest differences at the beta-sheet core interface with helices alpha2 and alpha3; N111 side chain differs between conformers (R18092-J4). Rex at I45, D54-G57, K63, N67, E134-A135 (R18092-J3).
fallback_annotation: May have a minor conformer (10-20%) in which helices alpha2 and alpha3, flanking the NIKS loop, change orientation relative to the beta-sheet core, based on doubled 15N-1H HSQC peaks of the free isolated N-domain at 298 K (doi:10.1002/pro.2067).
other_conditions: N-domain in the full-length human eRF1 crystal versus the isolated domain in solution: remote loops 29-33, 61-64 and 101-105 differ and are read as intrinsic; 115-123, 41-42 and 89-91 are likely construct effects; static, no rate (R18092-J6, R18092-J7, R18092-r4).

Mouse full-length eRF1 bound to MoMLV reverse transcriptase (5DMQ) and the mouse C-domain bound to RNase H (5DMR): other constructs and partners with no N-domain motion measured; not assessable (R18092-r5, R18092-r6).
caveats: One paper, one sample. No exchange cross-peaks, rate or full doubled-residue list is reported, and causes other than a conformational switch (proline isomerization, sample heterogeneity) were not tested, so the call rests on the authors' two-state reading of the doubled peaks. The sample is His6-tagged and in phosphate buffer, which this mRNA-binding domain might sense; no control exists. The 2LLX ensemble describes the major conformer only. Method searches used the card's viral identity, so other human eRF1 studies may exist.

protein: Human transforming growth factor alpha, mature 50-residue domain (V1-A50, UniProt P01135)
reference_state: Entry construct as deposited (mature human TGF-alpha V1-A50), free, no ligand; the RelaxDB source sample (doi:10.1021/bi00008a003, full text): 2 mM 15N protein dissolved directly in 90% H2O/10% D2O with 1 mM NaN3, no buffer stated, pH 7.1 ± 0.1, 30 ± 0.5 °C, 500 MHz, single field (HTGFA-J11 to J15 marked is_wt_apo).
literal_two_peak: does not: the source states that the exchange broadening reflects interconversion between multiple protein conformations on the intermediate 15N chemical-exchange (microsecond) timescale, with an author-derived lifetime between about 1.25 µs and 2.5 ms; no kex or Δω is printed (the bounds assume two equal populations and a maximum 10 ppm shift difference), so no regime can be computed, and no second peak set is reported for the free ligand (HTGFA-J12; E-r2). The title's 'slow conformational exchange' means slower than molecular tumbling. The only other stated regime, fast exchange, concerns EGFR-ED binding (HTGFA-J7).
basis: Reference state: in the RelaxDB source sample (free hTGF-alpha, pH 7.1, 30 °C, 500 MHz) 23 of 36 analysed backbone amides carry single-field exchange broadening above 0.5 Hz (D7-C8, T13-H18, T20-K29, C32-V33, V39-G40, E44-H45; fourteen above 1.5 Hz, largest R22 4.93 ± 0.74 s-1), concentrated at the interface between the N- and C-terminal subdomains and in the first-strand region; the authors read this as interconversion between multiple backbone conformations with a lifetime between about 1.25 µs and 2.5 ms and propose first-strand dissociation from the core sheet, inter-subdomain hinge bending and/or disulfide isomerisation, without resolving their contributions; a BPTI control showed little broadening except near its disulfide (HTGFA-J12, E-r2). Under the single-field Rex rule of 2026-10-20 this is exchange detected in the reference state without a population, so the call is 'possible'. No fitted rate, population, shift difference, dispersion series or second peak set exists; the authors say CPMG field-strength measurements were in progress. Fast motion is confined to the C-terminal tail and the N-terminal bend (HTGFA-J11, J13), and the C8-F15 loop disorder of the NMR ensemble is attributed partly to exchange broadening (HTGFA-J15). The other free-ligand evidence is abstract-level: flexible termini, a pH-dependent interconversion with no rate or regime, and partial disorder at pH 3.5 and 30 °C, a different sample state from pH 6.5.
kex: not fitted: single-field Rex > 0.5 Hz at 23 amides (uncertainties about ±0.3-0.5 Hz); author bounds on the exchange lifetime of about 1.25 µs (from a 10 ppm maximum 15N shift difference and a 0.5 Hz detection limit) to about 2.5 ms (from non-refocusing at CPMG 2tau = 720 µs), assuming two equally populated states (HTGFA-J12)
pB: not measured; two equally populated states are an assumption of the lifetime bounds, and the '40%' or 'about half' figure is the fraction of amides with exchange broadening, not a population (HTGFA-J12)
regime: Authors: intermediate 15N chemical-exchange (microsecond) timescale; lifetime bounded between about 1.25 µs and 2.5 ms; no kex or Δω printed, so no computed regime (HTGFA-J12). Not stated for the pH-dependent interconversion (HTGFA-J2, HTGFA-J3). EGFR-ED binding is in the fast-exchange limit (HTGFA-J7, binding kinetics).
residues: Rex > 0.5 Hz: D7, C8, T13, F15, C16, F17, H18, T20, C21, R22, F23, L24, V25, Q26, E27, D28, K29, C32, V33, V39, G40, E44, H45 (Q14 unfitted; S36, C43 below threshold; D47 term rejected); > 1.5 Hz at D7, T13, F15, C16, C21, R22, F23, L24, V25, K29, C32, V33, V39, G40 (Table 3, cycle C; largest R22 4.93, V39 3.81, C21 3.50 s-1); interface residues F15-H18, C32-V33, V39-G40, E44-H45 (HTGFA-J12). Fast motion: L48-A50, D7-C8, F17-H18, E27-D28, V39-G40, F23, A31 (HTGFA-J11).

structure_match.what: TGF-alpha bound to inactive IDE; aa 1-3 and 10-14 visible, D10-Q14 helix-to-strand versus free 1YUF. Partner-bound with possible incomplete occupancy, not an apo alternate state.
TGF-alpha-bound full-length EGFR cryo-EM classes (tips separated, tips juxtaposed); the heterogeneity is in the receptor. Partner-bound, not an apo alternate state.

fallback_annotation: May have alternate backbone conformations involving the interface between the N- and C-terminal subdomains (F15-H18, C32-V33, V39-G40, E44-H45) and the first beta-strand region (D7-C8, C21-V25): single-field 15N exchange broadening above 0.5 Hz at 23 amides of free TGF-alpha at pH 7.1, 30 °C, lifetime between about 1.25 µs and 2.5 ms, candidate mechanisms first-strand dissociation, subdomain hinge bending or disulfide isomerisation (doi:10.1021/bi00008a003); no rate or population; the pH-dependent interconversion is known only from an abstract (doi:10.1111/j.1432-1033.1991.tb16050.x).
other_conditions: pH 7.1 ± 0.1, 30 ± 0.5 °C, no buffer, 500 MHz, free ligand (1995 RelaxDB source, full text): possible. Single-field Rex > 0.5 Hz at 23 amides (interface and first-strand region), lifetime 1.25 µs to 2.5 ms, intermediate-exchange wording; fast motion at L48-A50 and D7-C8; water-saturation artefact shown for the presaturated HNOE reference (HTGFA-J11 to J15; E-r1 to r4).

pH 3.5, 30 °C versus pH 6.5, 10 or 30 °C: partially disordered at acidic pH with most hydrogen-bonded backbone intact; condition comparison from an abstract, no rate (HTGFA-J3, HTGFA-HTGFA_20261020092056-r9).
pH 3.5: amide exchange much faster than mouse EGF (HTGFA-J4, HTGFA-HTGFA_20261020092056-r1).
EGFR-ED bound: C terminus and interior immobilised, N terminus mobile; binding in fast exchange (HTGFA-J6, HTGFA-J7, HTGFA-HTGFA_20261020092056-r3).
Dried film after D2O vapour (ATR-FTIR), pH 7.4 HEPES/NaCl before drying: class H/D exchange rates 0.91, 0.27 and 1.41 x 10-4 min-1, not residue-resolved (HTGFA-J5, HTGFA-HTGFA_20261020092056-r10).
caveats: Call raised from unknown to possible on 2026-10-20 after the RelaxDB source paper (doi:10.1021/bi00008a003, Li and Montelione 1995) was read in full: exchange is detected in the reference state as single-field Rex at 23 of 36 analysed amides, and under the single-field Rex rule decided that night (ledger/redraft_notes.json, _RULE_single_field_rex) this counts as exchange detected without a population. Fixed caveat: single-field Rex can also come from anisotropic tumbling; a dispersion experiment would confirm. The authors themselves call the regime intermediate (microsecond) and give only lifetime bounds (1.25 µs to 2.5 ms) under an equal-population, 10 ppm assumption, so the state is not shown to be slow enough for separate peaks; literal_two_peak is 'does not'. The sample has no buffer (direct dissolution with NaN3), the Rex threshold of 0.5 Hz is the authors' operational cutoff with uncertainties of ±0.3-0.5 Hz, and Q26 lacks a reported error. Nine of the other rows are abstracts. The RelaxDB HTGFA source is still unconfirmed (no BMRB id). The abstract-only rows HTGFA-HTGFA_20261020145442-r1 and r2 are superseded and no longer cited. Built from cases V6_r6_HTGFA_20261020092056, S6_r6_HTGFA_20261020145442 and S6_r6_HTGFA_20261020201428.

protein: Human cellular retinoic acid-binding protein 2 (CRABP2, UniProt P29373), residues P1-E137
reference_state: Entry construct as deposited (human CRABP2 P1-E137, wild type), free, no retinoid; measured at 298 K, pH 7.4, 20 mM sodium phosphate, 150 mM NaCl, 5 mM DTT, 10% D2O, 1.0 mM, Thio6His6 tag removed by TEV (2019 paper)
literal_two_peak: does not: the authors describe the free-protein exchange as intermediate-timescale ('intermediate conformational exchange'), with broadened, unassignable amides near the exchanging residues; no second peak set is reported. The slow-exchange statement in the paper concerns atRA binding, not the apo state.
basis: Free wild-type CRABP2 shows microsecond-millisecond exchange across the portal and gap regions by two-field 15N CPMG, and a core group of residues fits one two-state process with a measured rate and a large minor-state population. The CPMG shifts do not match the atRA-bound shifts, so the minor state is a distinct apo conformation, not the holo structure. Other residues exchange at similar rates without sharing the fit, and atRA quenches the process.
kex: 320 ± 40 s-1 (core-group global Carver-Richards fit, 298 K, 800 and 900 MHz) (CRABP2-J1, CRABP2-r5)
pB: 0.2 ± 0.03 (CRABP2-J1, CRABP2-r5)
regime: Intermediate, as stated by the authors; per-residue delta omega is in Table S1, which was not retrieved, so the regime cannot be checked against kex.
residues: Core group K8, L19, L22, K30, I31, A32, R59, E73, Q74, V76, T114, T131, Y134, plus 'Thr51-Ile53' which does not map to the entry sequence (Y51-I52-K53) and is left out (CRABP2-J1). Further dispersing residues are shown only in Fig. 5B (CRABP2-J2); 14 amides broadened beyond assignment: E13, E16, R29, A34-A36, K38, V41, T56-V58, T60, N115, V133 (CRABP2-J3).

structure_match.what: atRA-bound crystal structure. The authors find the CPMG-derived shifts do not agree with the apo-to-holo CSPs, so the minor state is structurally distinct from the atRA complex; not a match.
Apo crystal structure; pocket near-identical to 2FR3, so it shows the dominant conformer, not the CPMG minor state.

fallback_annotation: May have an alternate apo conformation involving the portal (alpha1-loop-alpha2, betaC-betaD and betaE-betaF loops) and gap (betaD, betaE) regions, based on 15N CPMG relaxation dispersion of the free protein (doi:10.1021/acs.biochem.9b00672); the 1998 apo NMR ensemble with a widened ligand entrance (doi:10.1021/bi9808924, abstract only) is a candidate but is not tied to the CPMG state.
other_conditions: atRA-bound, same buffer, 298 K, 1.0 mM: core exchange not detected by CPMG (CRABP2-J4, CRABP2-r7); residual faster fluctuation at I10-S12, L19, K38, T122-T124, R132, unresolved because four of these residues lie on the dimer interface (CRABP2-J5, CRABP2-r8).
atRA-bound, pH 6.8, 10-800 μM: weak self-association, apparent Kd about 1.0 ± 0.2 mM; intermolecular, not an alternate state (CRABP2-J12, CRABP2-r10).
His6-tagged CRABP2 on an SPR chip, 25 °C, Tween 20: atRA kon (6.92 ± 2.32) x 10^5 M-1 s-1, koff (4.01 ± 1.08) x 10^-3 s-1; binding kinetics (CRABP2-J13, CRABP2-r11).
caveats: One paper, one temperature (298 K), phosphate buffer without a phosphate-free control, 1.0 mM protein; the supplement (Table S1, Figs. S4, S6) was not retrieved, so per-residue delta omega and the CPMG-versus-CSP comparison could not be checked. The core list contains a residue range that does not fit the entry sequence. A minor-state population of 0.2 is large for a CPMG fit and has no second method behind it. The RelaxDB CRABP2 source sample is unknown (no BMRB id). Built from case V6_r6_CRABP2_20261020094132; replaces the empty search_insufficient judgment of the crashed first search.

protein: Escherichia coli / Salmonella typhi thioredoxin-1 (TrxA; entry sequence UniProt P0AA29 without Met1, identical to E. coli P0AA25), wild type, 108 residues
reference_state: Wild-type thioredoxin-1 as deposited (108-residue mature sequence), free, no ligand. Redox form is a sample state: the RelaxDB card gives no BMRB id, no redox state and links only the oxidized human-E. coli chimera 1M7T, so the deposited form is unknown; the call is given for each form. The key solution study (Stone et al. 1993, doi:10.1021/bi00053a007, now full text) measured both forms at 308 K on a 500 MHz spectrometer (single field, 1.0 ms CPMG spacing); its main text does not state protein concentration, buffer, pH or solvent isotope fraction (TRX-J1, J2, J15, J16, J51 marked is_wt_apo).
literal_two_peak: cannot tell for NMR: the 1993 source states no exchange regime, prints no kex, population or Δω and reports no second peak set for either redox form; exchange is single-field model-free Rex above 1.5 Hz (reduced: G33, I38, I45, R73, G74, I75, W31 indole; oxidized: W31 indole, I45), which the authors call microsecond-millisecond mobility (TRX-J15, J51). The oxidized-form active-site millisecond motion of 1996 is a transient conformation in an abstract (TRX-J17). The 1989 urea-gradient abstract states slow (minute-scale) interconversion of cis and trans P76 forms in folded reduced thioredoxin with less than a few percent trans, but it is electrophoresis read from an abstract, not an NMR peak count, and the 1993 authors exclude P76 isomerisation as the source of the 73-75 broadening (TRX-J29).
basis: Possible for both redox forms under the single-field Rex rule of 2026-10-20: exchange is detected in the reference state without a population. Reduced form (dithiol): the 1993 full text reports exchange broadening significantly above 1.5 Hz at G33, I38, I45, R73, G74, I75 and the W31 indole, read as microsecond-millisecond mobility propagated from I75 to R73-G74 and as greater flexibility around the active site in the reduced protein, explicitly not P76 cis-trans isomerisation (TRX-J15; E-r4); no kex, population or Δω. Oxidized form (C32-C35 disulfide): the same study finds broadening above 1.5 Hz only at the W31 indole and I45 (TRX-J51; E-r3) and none at R73-I75 (TRX-J16, no_evidence_in_window), while the 1996 13C/15N relaxation abstract reports millisecond motion at nuclei around the active-site disulfide interpreted as a strained transient disulfide conformation (TRX-J17; 101601-r5, abstract only). No CPMG, R1rho or CEST measurement exists for either form (TRX-J21). Supporting but not reference-state: the reassembled 1-73/74-108 solid-state construct loses G21, P40, T54 and R73 on cooling to 238 K (TRX-J12); the E101G crystal refines a 50/50 alternate backbone over 10-25, 77-91 and 95-107 (TRX-J35); wild-type MD makes persistent transitions at 13-18 (TRX-J38); native-state HX of oxidized wild type finds no partially unfolded form below global unfolding at 24 probes (TRX-J30).
kex: not reported for either redox form; Rex above 1.5 Hz (values figure-only, Figure 3E/F; W31 indole 4.0 ± 0.2 Hz oxidized and 2.8 ± 0.1 Hz reduced, W28 0.44 ± 0.02 Hz oxidized, Table I) at the sites listed, from single-field model-free fitting with a 1.0 ms CPMG spacing (TRX-J15, J51); the 1996 oxidized active-site millisecond motion is stated without values (TRX-J17, abstract)
pB: not reported for either redox form (TRX-J15, J51, J17)
regime: not stated in the 1993 full text; no Δω printed; the authors speak of microsecond-to-millisecond mobility and exclude P76 cis-trans isomerisation on timescale grounds. The oxidized-form 73-75 result is 'no significant exchange broadening' by the same Rex analysis (TRX-J16).
residues: Reduced: W31 indole, G33, I38, I45, R73, G74, I75 (Rex > 1.5 Hz; TRX-J15). Oxidized: W31 indole, I45 (TRX-J51); R73-I75 quiet (TRX-J16); G33 not measurable (TRX-J52). Oxidized 1996: nuclei around the active-site disulfide C32-C35, not enumerated in the abstract (TRX-J17). Solid-state reassembly (other construct, 238 K): G21, P40, T54, R73 lost; A19, D20, G21, R73 survive the T2' filter (TRX-J12).

structure_match.what: Oxidized wild-type crystal (1.68 Å) with ten unnamed residues in two alternative conformations and differences between the two independent molecules that may reflect crystal contacts; residues 29-37 form a surface protrusion. A crystal alternative, not a solved minor state.

E101G mutant crystal: chain B refines as two complete backbone conformers (Ba/Bb, 50% each) over D10-V25, T77-V91 and S95-L107, read by the authors as members of the native-like ensemble. Mutant, Cu(II)/ethanol crystal, no solution population; not tied to the 73-75 or active-site exchange.

Oxidized human-E. coli chimera linked by the RelaxDB card; its 15N relaxation gives S2 0.88 with mobile loops 72-74 and 92-94 (chimera numbering). A homolog construct, not the entry sequence and not a minor state.

fallback_annotation: May have an alternate apo conformation around the active site: in the reduced (dithiol) form single-field 15N exchange broadening above 1.5 Hz at G33, I38, I45, R73, G74, I75 and the W31 indole at 308 K, and in the oxidized form at the W31 indole and I45 (doi:10.1021/bi00053a007, full text); in the oxidized form also millisecond motion around the C32-C35 disulfide interpreted as a strained transient disulfide conformation (doi:10.1021/ja960877r, abstract only). The alternative conformers of the wild-type crystal 2TRX and the E101G crystal 5HR0 are candidates without a rate or population.
other_conditions: Reassembled 1-73/74-108 E. coli thioredoxin, hydrated PEG-4000 precipitate, 288 K to 238 K, MAS NMR: possible. Cooling removes G21, P40, T54 and R73 and broadens most other peaks (10-100 microsecond interference, static heterogeneity not excluded); G21 shows CSA averaging faster than about 100 microseconds (TRX-J11, TRX-J12; 101601-r8, r9, r10).
Reassembled construct by DARR below -15 °C: intermediate-timescale motion reported without residues (TRX-J13; 101601-r31, abstract).
Fragment complex TRX1-93 + TRX94-108: elevated R2 at 43-50 and 74-89 attributed to peptide-modulated exchange, no rate (TRX-J18; 101601-r19, abstract).
L78K core mutant: greater exchange contribution than wild type, no values (TRX-J19; 101601-r34, abstract).
Oxidized wild type, 25 °C, pH 7, 30 mM phosphate, 0.1 M KCl, native-state HX: no partially unfolded form at 24 probes; delta-G of opening 4.7-9.9 kcal/mol (TRX-J30; 101601-r28, r29).
Wild type reduced, 20 °C, pH 7.0, Tris, 1 mM DTT, 600 MHz: R1/R2/NOE profile figure only, no exchange analysis (TRX-J9; TRX-r40).

Wild type, both redox forms, urea-gradient electrophoresis at 2 and 25 °C: two compact forms assigned to cis/trans I75-P76; in the folded reduced form they interconvert slowly on the minute time scale with less than a few percent trans without urea, the oxidized form is essentially all cis (TRX-J29; 101601-r21, r22, r27, abstracts; not NMR, no rate constant). The 1993 relaxation paper states that the 73-75 broadening cannot be P76 isomerisation because that would be much slower.
